1	---
2	name: compose-recomposition-performance
3	description: Use when investigating Jetpack Compose recomposition performance, skippable/restartable composables, composables.txt or compiler reports, Layout Inspector recomposition counts, back-writing snapshot state across phases, or frame-rate State reads in composition vs layout/draw, and it is not yet clear whether the cause is parameter stability, deferred reads, or cross-phase back-writing.
4	---
5	
6	# Compose recomposition performance
7	
8	Router only — deep fixes live in focused skills below.
9	
10	## Three axes
11	
12	1. **Parameter stability / skipping** — can Compose skip this restartable composable; are arguments stable and comparable?
13	2. **Where `State` is read** — is frame-rate `State` read during composition vs layout/draw?
14	3. **Back-writing across phases** — does a later phase write snapshot state that invalidates an earlier phase? Examples: map/list mutation during composition that re-invalidates the same composition; `onSizeChanged` (layout phase) writing state read by a sibling in composition.
15	
16	Axes 2 and 3 often overlap (a sibling reading measured size in composition is both a deferred-read violation and a layout → composition back-write). Axis 1 is independent.
17	
18	## Route here → focused skill
19	
20	| Primary suspicion | Next skill |
21	|---|---|
22	| Skipping, unstable params, compiler/`composables.txt` churn | [`compose-stability-diagnostics`](../compose-stability-diagnostics/SKILL.md) |
23	| Frame-rate `State` read phase (composition vs layout/draw) | [`compose-state-deferred-reads`](../compose-state-deferred-reads/SKILL.md) |
24	| `putAll` / map rebuild / cross-row `height(state)` during composition | [`compose-state-deferred-reads`](../compose-state-deferred-reads/SKILL.md) — § back-writing |
25	| Focus-driven side work in composable body | [`compose-side-effects`](../compose-side-effects/SKILL.md) — `snapshotFlow` |
26	| Evidence for multiple axes | Apply matching skills in parallel |
27	
28	## Review order
29	
30	1. Reproduce one transition (focus move, insertion, scroll) and note which composables recompose.
31	2. If counts spike on unchanged lazy items, check back-writing (composition mutations and cross-row measurement) before blaming stability.
32	3. If counts climb every frame during scroll/animation, check deferred reads.
33	4. If skipping fails despite stable data, check parameter stability and compiler reports.
34	5. Re-measure after each fix.
35	
36	## False leads
37	
38	These changes often **do not** reduce recomposition count:
39	
40	| Attempt | Why it fails |
41	|---|---|
42	| `remember(index) { isFirstRow(index) }` instead of inline `when (index)` | Same inputs; no skipping benefit |
43	| Identity cache for read-only derived maps | Can serve stale overlays; `remember(keys)` is enough |
44	| `mutableIntStateOf` + layout modifier on **both** measured and sibling rows | Sibling still reads size in composition unless measure-only |
45	| Forcing `Exactly(1)` on both rows in focus-move tests | One row often correctly recomposes 0 times |
46	| Hoisting without stabilizing lambda captures | New lambda instance each frame still defeats skipping |
47	
48	## When NOT to apply
49	
50	- Recomposition tracks real data changes, or the bug is correctness not cost.
51	- No profiler / compiler signal suggests a problem.
52	
53	## Related
54	
55	- [`compose-state-authoring`](../compose-state-authoring/SKILL.md) — authoring `mutableState*` safely.
56

1	---
2	name: compose-side-effects
3	description: Use when writing or reviewing Jetpack Compose code with LaunchedEffect, DisposableEffect, SideEffect, rememberCoroutineScope, rememberUpdatedState, snapshotFlow, snackbar, navigation, focus requests, analytics, or event Flow collection.
4	---
5	
6	# Compose: side effects
7	
8	## Core principle
9	
10	Composable bodies describe UI. They can be recomposed, skipped, or abandoned. Work that changes the outside world belongs in an effect API whose lifecycle matches the work.
11	
12	## Pick the smallest effect
13	
14	| Need | API |
15	|---|---|
16	| Publish Compose state to non-Compose code after every successful recomposition | `SideEffect` |
17	| Register/unregister a listener, callback, observer, or resource | `DisposableEffect(keys...)` |
18	| Run suspending, deferred, or keyed one-shot work | `LaunchedEffect(keys...)` |
19	| Launch suspending work from a user event callback | `rememberCoroutineScope()` |
20	| Convert Compose snapshot reads into a Flow inside a coroutine | `snapshotFlow { ... }` inside `LaunchedEffect` |
21	
22	## Effect keys
23	
24	Keys define restart identity. When any key changes, the old effect is cancelled/disposed and a new one starts.
25	
26	```kotlin
27	// ✅ Restart collection when userId changes
28	LaunchedEffect(userId) {
29	    repository.events(userId).collect { event -> handle(event) }
30	}
31	
32	// ❌ Unit hides a changing input; collection keeps using the first userId
33	LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
34	    repository.events(userId).collect { event -> handle(event) }
35	}
36	```
37	
38	Use stable, semantic keys:
39	
40	- Use the thing whose lifecycle the effect follows: `userId`, `screenId`, `lifecycleOwner`, `focusRequester`.
41	- Do not use broad objects (`state`, `viewModel`) when only one property matters.
42	- Do not add changing lambdas as keys unless you really want restarts on every lambda change.
43	
44	## Avoid stale captures
45	
46	For long-running effects that should not restart but need the latest callback or value, use `rememberUpdatedState`.
47	
48	```kotlin
49	@Composable
50	fun Timeout(onTimeout: () -> Unit) {
51	    val latestOnTimeout by rememberUpdatedState(onTimeout)
52	
53	    LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
54	        delay(1_000)
55	        latestOnTimeout()
56	    }
57	}
58	```
59	
60	Use this when the lifecycle is "start once" but the invoked lambda should stay fresh. Common cases:
61	
62	- A timeout or splash effect should not restart when `onTimeout` changes, but it should call the latest callback.
63	- A lifecycle observer should stay registered to the same owner, but invoke the latest `onStart` / `onStop` lambdas.
64	- A long-running collector should keep its collection lifecycle, but call the latest event handler.
65	
66	Do not use `rememberUpdatedState` to avoid choosing proper keys. If the changed value should restart the work, make it a key instead:
67	
68	```kotlin
69	// BAD: userId changes should restart the collection, not update a captured value.
70	val latestUserId by rememberUpdatedState(userId)
71	LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
72	    repository.events(latestUserId).collect { event -> handle(event) }
73	}
74	
75	// GOOD: the collection lifecycle follows userId.
76	LaunchedEffect(userId) {
77	    repository.events(userId).collect { event -> handle(event) }
78	}
79	```
80	
81	### `rememberUpdatedState` values are stale inside `remember {}` blocks
82	
83	`rememberUpdatedState` returns a `State` object whose `.value` is updated on every recomposition. The "latest" behavior only helps when the State is **read lazily** — inside an effect body or a lambda that runs later — not when the value is captured eagerly.
84	
85	Inside a `remember {}` block the producer lambda runs once. Reading the delegate there snapshots the current `.value` into the remembered object — future State updates never reach it:
86	
87	```kotlin
88	val latestChannelId by rememberUpdatedState(channelId)
89	
90	// ❌ BAD — channelId is read once when remember's lambda executes;
91	// the destination holds the initial value forever
92	val destination = remember {
93	    Destination(channelId = latestChannelId)
94	}
95	
96	// ✅ GOOD — skip rememberUpdatedState; key remember on the changing value
97	val destination = remember(channelId) {
98	    Destination(channelId = channelId)
99	}
100	
101	// ✅ ALSO GOOD — wrapping lambda defers the read to each invocation
102	val destination = remember {
103	    Destination(channelId = { latestChannelId })
104	}
105	```
106	
107	The same trap applies anywhere a `rememberUpdatedState` delegate is **read eagerly** rather than deferred behind a lambda or effect body: data classes constructed in `remember`, objects built once in `DisposableEffect`'s setup block, or any expression evaluated at creation time.
108	
109	When the captured value should trigger recreation of the remembered object, make it a `remember` key and skip `rememberUpdatedState` entirely. Reserve `rememberUpdatedState` for values that must stay fresh inside a long-lived scope (effect coroutine, event callback) **without** restarting that scope.
110	
111	`rememberUpdatedState` also does not make render state "non-recomposing." If the UI needs to display a changing value, read normal `State` in composition or use the deferred-read patterns in [`compose-state-deferred-reads`](../compose-state-deferred-reads/SKILL.md) for frame-rate values.
112	
113	## Collecting Flow
114	
115	Use `LaunchedEffect` for **side-effect/event flows**: snackbars, navigation events, analytics events, focus commands, or other streams where each emission triggers imperative work.
116	
117	```kotlin
118	LaunchedEffect(events) {
119	    events.collect { event ->
120	        snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(event.message)
121	    }
122	}
123	```
124	
125	Do not collect render state imperatively just to mutate local state. For UI state, collect near the state holder and pass plain values into the UI composable—the **state-holder vs UI split**, `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` / `collectAsState()`, and preview-friendly wiring are covered in [`compose-state-holder-ui-split`](../compose-state-holder-ui-split/SKILL.md). Do not duplicate that architecture here.
126	
127	On Android, prefer lifecycle-aware collection where available; use `collectAsState()` on targets without lifecycle-aware APIs.
128	
129	For Compose state reads, use `snapshotFlow`:
130	
131	```kotlin
132	LaunchedEffect(listState) {
133	    snapshotFlow { listState.firstVisibleItemIndex }
134	        .distinctUntilChanged()
135	        .collect { index -> analytics.visibleIndex(index) }
136	}
137	```
138	
139	`snapshotFlow { ... }.map { ... }` without a terminal `collect` does nothing.
140	
141	## User events
142	
143	Use `rememberCoroutineScope()` when a click or gesture starts suspending work:
144	
145	```kotlin
146	@Composable
147	fun SaveButton(snackbarHostState: SnackbarHostState) {
148	    val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
149	
150	    Button(
151	        onClick = {
152	            scope.launch {
153	                snackbarHostState.showSnackbar("Saved")
154	            }
155	        },
156	    ) {
157	        Text("Save")
158	    }
159	}
160	```
161	
162	Avoid "event flag" state just to trigger a `LaunchedEffect`. The click already is the event.
163	
164	## Registration and cleanup
165	
166	Use `DisposableEffect` for paired setup/teardown:
167	
168	```kotlin
169	@Composable
170	fun ObserveLifecycle(owner: LifecycleOwner, observer: LifecycleObserver) {
171	    DisposableEffect(owner, observer) {
172	        owner.lifecycle.addObserver(observer)
173	        onDispose {
174	            owner.lifecycle.removeObserver(observer)
175	        }
176	    }
177	}
178	```
179	
180	Every registration path should have a matching `onDispose` cleanup path.
181	
182	## Common mistakes
183	
184	| Mistake | Diagnosis | Fix |
185	|---|---|---|
186	| Network request directly in the composable body | Side work in composition | Usually move to a ViewModel/state holder; use `LaunchedEffect` only for UI-owned keyed work |
187	| Analytics property written from the composable body | Side work in composition | Use `SideEffect` when it should publish after every successful recomposition |
188	| Impression/event logged from the composable body | Side work in composition | Use `LaunchedEffect(key)` when it should run once for that key |
189	| `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` captures changing `id` | Missing key | Key by `id`, or use `rememberUpdatedState` if it must not restart |
190	| `rememberUpdatedState(id)` used so `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` keeps running after `id` changes | Hidden lifecycle bug | Key the effect by `id` |
191	| Long-lived effect invokes an old callback after recomposition | Stale capture | Wrap the callback with `rememberUpdatedState` and call the wrapper inside the effect |
192	| `rememberUpdatedState` delegate read directly in `remember {}` (e.g. `Destination(id = latestId)`) | Value captured once, never refreshed | Make the value a `remember` key: `remember(id) { Destination(id = id) }` |
193	| `LaunchedEffect(state) { ... }` restarts too often | Overly broad key | Key by the specific property |
194	| `LaunchedEffect(...) { nonSuspendSetter() }` | Wrong effect type | Usually `SideEffect`; keep `LaunchedEffect` only for keyed one-shot/deferred work |
195	| Listener added in `LaunchedEffect` with no cleanup | Missing disposal | Use `DisposableEffect` |
196	| Launching from click by setting `shouldShowSnackbar = true` | Event flag anti-pattern | Use `rememberCoroutineScope()` in the click callback |
197	| `if (isFocused) { … }` or focus read in composable body for side work | Side work during composition | `LaunchedEffect(focused) { … }` or `snapshotFlow` |
198	| `onSizeChanged { heightState = it.height }` on measured composable | Layout → composition back-write if a sibling reads `heightState` in composition | Siblings must consume height in measure phase, not `Modifier.height(state.dp)` in composition |
199	
200	## Focus and measurement
201	
202	**Focus:** Reading focus in the composable body to drive **side work** (preloading, analytics, toasts) runs that work during composition. Observe focus in an effect instead:
203	
204	```kotlin
205	// ❌ BAD — side work runs during composition every time `focused` is true,
206	// including transient focus passes; `SideEffect` re-runs after every successful recomposition
207	@Composable
208	fun Preloader(interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource) {
209	    val focused by interactionSource.collectIsFocusedAsState()
210	    if (focused) {
211	        preloadImages()
212	    }
213	}
214	
215	// ✅ GOOD — side work in a keyed effect
216	@Composable
217	fun Preloader(interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource) {
218	    val focused by interactionSource.collectIsFocusedAsState()
219	    LaunchedEffect(focused) {
220	        if (focused) preloadImages()
221	    }
222	}
223	```
224	
225	Use `snapshotFlow { … }` inside `LaunchedEffect` when you need to sample multiple snapshot reads or debounce rapid changes without keying the effect on every derived value. For TV/D-pad focus navigation semantics, see [`compose-focus-navigation`](../compose-focus-navigation/SKILL.md).
226	
227	**Measurement:** `onSizeChanged` / `onGloballyPositioned` are valid **callbacks**, but they fire during the layout phase. Writing snapshot state there is only safe if no earlier phase reads it. If a sibling reads that state in composition, layout is back-writing into composition and the sibling will recompose every measure pass. Apply captured dimensions in `Modifier.layout` (see [`compose-modifier-and-layout-style`](../compose-modifier-and-layout-style/SKILL.md) §7 and [`compose-state-deferred-reads`](../compose-state-deferred-reads/SKILL.md)).
228	
229	## Red flags during review
230	
231	- "This only runs once" about code in a composable body.
232	- `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` in a function with changing parameters.
233	- A flow chain inside an effect with no terminal collection.
234	- Effects whose keys are chosen to silence lint instead of model lifecycle.
235	- Callback lambdas used from long-lived effects without either a key or `rememberUpdatedState`.
236	- `rememberUpdatedState` delegate read eagerly inside a `remember {}` block or object constructor — the value is captured once and never refreshes.
237

1	---
2	name: compose-slot-api-pattern
3	description: Use when designing or reviewing a reusable Jetpack Compose component whose visual regions vary by caller, or when primitive content parameters and boolean shape flags are accumulating.
4	---
5	
6	# Compose: slot API pattern
7	
8	## Core principle
9	
10	A reusable Compose component describes layout structure. Callers provide variable visual content through slots.
11	
12	## API review procedure
13	
14	1. Confirm the component is reusable. For a true single-use composable, do not add slot ceremony.
15	2. Mark which regions vary by caller: headline, supporting text, leading visual, trailing visual, actions, body.
16	3. Replace caller-controlled primitive content and shape flags with slots.
17	4. Add receiver scopes only when the slot is emitted inside a layout whose scope APIs callers should use.
18	5. Make absent optional regions nullable (`null`), so the component can omit their containers and spacing.
19	6. Put repeated default content or tokens in `XxxDefaults`.
20	7. Pair this with the `modifier` rules in `compose-modifier-and-layout-style`.
21	
22	## 1. Replace primitive content with `@Composable` slots
23	
24	Where the component asks for caller-controlled *content*, prefer a `@Composable () -> Unit` slot. Where the slot is structurally required, leave it non-nullable with no default. Where it's optional, make it nullable with a `null` default.
25	
26	```kotlin
27	// ❌ BAD — primitive parameters; trailing area is the only slot; everything else is locked
28	@Composable
29	fun SettingsRow(
30	    title: String,
31	    onClick: () -> Unit,
32	    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
33	    subtitle: String? = null,
34	    leadingIcon: ImageVector? = null,
35	    trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
36	) { … }
37	```
38	
39	```kotlin
40	// ✅ GOOD — every visual region is a slot; the row describes structure, not content
41	@Composable
42	fun SettingsRow(
43	    headlineContent: @Composable () -> Unit,
44	    onClick: () -> Unit,
45	    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
46	    supportingContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
47	    leadingContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
48	    trailingContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
49	) { … }
50	```
51	
52	Call sites stay short when the typical content is a one-liner:
53	
54	```kotlin
55	SettingsRow(
56	    headlineContent = { Text("Account") },
57	    leadingContent = { Icon(Icons.Default.Person, contentDescription = null) },
58	    trailingContent = { SettingsRowDefaults.Chevron() },
59	    onClick = { … },
60	)
61	```
62	
63	The unusual cases no longer require new component parameters:
64	
65	```kotlin
66	SettingsRow(
67	    headlineContent = {
68	        Row(verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
69	            Text("Inbox")
70	            Spacer(Modifier.width(8.dp))
71	            Badge { Text("3") }
72	        }
73	    },
74	    onClick = { … },
75	)
76	```
77	
78	### Slot naming
79	
80	- Use `xxxContent` for free-form `@Composable () -> Unit` slots (`headlineContent`, `supportingContent`, `trailingContent`) — matches Material 3.
81	- Use a singular noun (`title`, `icon`, `actions`) when the slot is semantically constrained and the component name disambiguates (`Scaffold(topBar = { … }, bottomBar = { … }, floatingActionButton = { … })`).
82	- Don't use `content` *and* other `xxxContent` slots together — pick one convention per component.
83	
84	## 2. Scope receivers when the slot emits into a layout
85	
86	If the slot's content will sit inside a `Row`/`Column`/`Box` whose layout features (`Modifier.weight`, `BoxScope.matchParentSize`, alignment) should be available to the caller, declare the slot as a receiver lambda: `@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit`.
87	
88	```kotlin
89	// ❌ BAD — actions render inside a Row, but callers can't use RowScope.weight()
90	@Composable
91	fun MyTopBar(
92	    title: @Composable () -> Unit,
93	    actions: @Composable () -> Unit = {},   // ← caller has no Row scope
94	)
95	```
96	
97	```kotlin
98	// ✅ GOOD — caller gets RowScope; .weight() and alignment-by works inside
99	@Composable
100	fun MyTopBar(
101	    title: @Composable () -> Unit,
102	    actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit = {},
103	)
104	```
105	
106	This is what makes `TopAppBar(actions = { IconButton(…); IconButton(…) })` work — the caller is implicitly inside a `RowScope`.
107	
108	Don't bolt a scope receiver onto every slot reflexively. The receiver should match the actual parent layout the slot emits into. If the slot is rendered inside a `Box`, use `BoxScope`. If it's inside a `Column`, use `ColumnScope`. If the parent is not a standard layout (or none of its scope APIs are useful in slot content), no receiver.
109	
110	## 3. Optional slots — nullable with `null` default
111	
112	For slots that may be absent, prefer `(@Composable () -> Unit)? = null` over `@Composable () -> Unit = {}`:
113	
114	```kotlin
115	// ❌ BAD — empty default; "no leading content" is the empty lambda
116	leadingContent: @Composable () -> Unit = {}
117	
118	// ✅ GOOD — null means "no slot"; the component can omit space/padding when absent
119	leadingContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null
120	```
121	
122	With a nullable slot, the component can branch on `leadingContent != null` and skip the slot's container, spacing, and padding entirely. With an empty default, the layout often still allocates space for absent content.
123	
124	## 4. Defaults live in `XxxDefaults`
125	
126	When you find yourself documenting "the trailing slot should usually be a chevron" or "pass `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface` for the default background", co-locate the helpers in a `XxxDefaults` object next to the component:
127	
128	```kotlin
129	object SettingsRowDefaults {
130	    @Composable
131	    fun Chevron() = Icon(
132	        imageVector = Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.KeyboardArrowRight,
133	        contentDescription = null,
134	    )
135	
136	    @Composable
137	    fun TrailingValue(text: String) = Text(
138	        text = text,
139	        style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium,
140	        color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
141	    )
142	}
143	```
144	
145	Call sites stay declarative for the common cases and the slot is still fully open for one-offs:
146	
147	```kotlin
148	SettingsRow(
149	    headlineContent = { Text("Notifications") },
150	    trailingContent = { SettingsRowDefaults.Chevron() },
151	    onClick = { … },
152	)
153	```
154	
155	This matches Material 3's `ButtonDefaults`, `TopAppBarDefaults`, etc. — defaults that are themselves composable belong here, not as new component parameters with `MaterialTheme.x.y` defaults expanded inline.
156	
157	## Quick reference
158	
159	| Symptom | Diagnosis | Fix |
160	|---|---|---|
161	| `title: String, subtitle: String?, leadingIcon: ImageVector?` on a reusable component | Primitive content params (§1) | Convert to `xxxContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)?` slots |
162	| Multiple boolean flags (`showChevron`, `showSwitch`) selecting trailing shapes | Enumerating shapes (§1) | One `trailingContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)?` slot |
163	| A `mode: Mode.Sealed` parameter listing variants | Same as flag soup (§1) | Slot it |
164	| `actions: @Composable () -> Unit = {}` inside a `Row` body | Missing scope receiver (§2) | `actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit = {}` |
165	| `slot: @Composable () -> Unit = {}` for an optional area | Empty-lambda default (§3) | `slot: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null` and branch on it |
166	| Component param `defaultColor: Color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface` | Defaults inlined (§4) | Move to `XxxDefaults.color` and reference it |
167	| Common trailing content repeats at every call site | Missing default helper (§4) | Add `XxxDefaults.Chevron()` etc. |
168	
169	## When NOT to apply
170	
171	- **Single-use components.** A composable used in exactly one place, with no plan to reuse, doesn't benefit from slot flexibility — and the slot indirection makes the code harder to read for the one reader. Primitive params + inline content is fine. (As soon as a second call site appears, slot it.)
172	- **Design-system primitives where every caller must look identical.** A `Heading2(text: String)` exists *because* you want every H2 to look the same; making it `headlineContent: @Composable () -> Unit` invites callers to break the rule. Keep it primitive. (Conversely: if `Heading2` ever needs a badge inline, slot it.)
173	- **Semantic parameters the component intentionally owns.** If the component owns typography, iconography, accessibility wording, or product consistency, a primitive parameter may be the constraint you want.
174	- **Constrained-type parameters that genuinely are constrained.** A `Switch(checked: Boolean, onCheckedChange: ...)` doesn't need its checked indicator to be a slot. Booleans-with-callbacks are not "content."
175	- **Performance-critical fast paths** (rare in app code; common in framework primitives). A slot is an allocated lambda. In the deepest LazyList item layer, sometimes primitives win. If you're not writing the framework, this doesn't apply.
176	
177	## Red flags during review
178	
179	| Thought | Reality |
180	|---|---|
181	| "Title is *always* a String — making it a slot is over-engineering" | "Always today" is the trap. Material's `ListItem.headlineContent` exists because tomorrow someone wants a `Text + Badge`. The slot is `8` characters of extra wrapping at every call site (`{ Text(…) }`); the refactor to add a slot later edits every existing call site. |
182	| "Lambdas are heavier than strings" | At the scale of typical Compose UI, this isn't measurable — and the framework's own components (`Button`, `ListItem`, `TopAppBar`, `Scaffold`) all slot. If your component is in the hottest of hot paths, see "When NOT to apply." |
183	| "I'll add a slot later if someone asks" | The slot turns one parameter into two parameters (the slot itself + maybe an internal flag) and edits every call site. The shape change isn't a "later" change. |
184	| "I'll model the variants with a sealed `Trailing` type instead" | Sealed enumeration is bounded; slots are unbounded. A sealed type works *until* the day someone needs a variant you didn't anticipate — at which point you're back to editing the component. The slot avoids the cycle. |
185	| "The leading area is *always* an icon, the trailing area varies — I'll slot only the trailing" | This is the partial-slot trap. The "always-an-icon" assumption breaks the first time a row needs an avatar or a flag emoji or a coloured shape. Slot leading too. |
186	| "There's only one call site today" | If there's only one call site, you're probably not designing a reusable component yet. See "When NOT to apply" — primitives are fine for a true single-use. The moment you copy-paste it, slot it. |
187	
188	## Related
189	
190	- [`compose-modifier-and-layout-style`](../compose-modifier-and-layout-style/SKILL.md) — the modifier-parameter rule (§1–§3 there) travels with slot APIs. A reusable component takes a `modifier` parameter *and* slots its content; the caller owns both placement and what to place.
191

1	---
2	name: compose-stability-diagnostics
3	description: Use when writing or reviewing Jetpack Compose parameter stability, compiler reports, skippability, unstable UI state classes, collection parameters, or Kotlin 2.0+ strong skipping behavior.
4	---
5	
6	# Compose stability diagnostics
7	
8	## Core principle
9	
10	Compose parameter fixes start from evidence. First identify the compiler mode and the parameter comparison behavior, then change the model or call site that is actually defeating skipping.
11	
12	With Kotlin 2.0.20+ strong skipping is enabled by default. Unstable parameters no longer automatically make restartable composables non-skippable, but unstable parameters compare by instance identity (`===`) while stable parameters compare by equality (`equals`). Churny unstable instances can still defeat skipping.
13	
14	## Diagnostic procedure
15	
16	1. Confirm the symptom: recomposition counts, compiler report output, or a suspected churny parameter.
17	2. Identify compiler mode: Kotlin/Compose compiler version and whether strong skipping is enabled.
18	3. Generate or read the Compose compiler reports for the shipped variant.
19	4. For each suspicious parameter, decide whether the problem is stability semantics, instance churn, or a caller-created lambda/derived value.
20	5. Apply the lightest fix that makes the type/call site truthful.
21	6. Re-measure the same interaction or re-read the same report before claiming the issue is fixed.
22	
23	## 1. Interpret strong skipping first
24	
25	On Kotlin 2.0.20+, strong skipping is enabled by default. In that mode:
26	
27	- Restartable composables are skippable even when parameters are unstable, unless explicitly opted out.
28	- Stable parameters compare with `equals`.
29	- Unstable parameters compare with instance equality (`===`).
30	- Lambdas inside composables are automatically remembered based on captures.
31	
32	Ask: "will these parameters compare the way I expect, and are callers creating new unstable instances every frame?"
33	
34	For older compiler setups or strong skipping disabled, the legacy rule still matters: a restartable composable with unstable parameters may be restartable but not skippable.
35	
36	## 2. Generate compiler reports
37	
38	With Kotlin 2.0+ the Compose Compiler is configured through the Kotlin Gradle plugin:
39	
40	```kotlin
41	plugins {
42	    alias(libs.plugins.android.application) // or android.library / jvm
43	    alias(libs.plugins.kotlin.android)      // or kotlin.multiplatform / kotlin.jvm
44	    alias(libs.plugins.compose.compiler)
45	}
46	
47	if (providers.gradleProperty("composeReports").orNull == "true") {
48	    composeCompiler {
49	        reportsDestination = layout.buildDirectory.dir("compose_compiler")
50	        metricsDestination = layout.buildDirectory.dir("compose_compiler")
51	    }
52	}
53	```
54	
55	Then build the variant whose compiler configuration you care about, for example:
56	
57	```bash
58	./gradlew :app:assembleRelease -PcomposeReports=true
59	```
60	
61	Use release/non-debuggable builds for runtime profiling. Compiler reports are build-time outputs, so the important thing is matching the variant and compiler flags you ship.
62	
63	Key files:
64	
65	| File | What it tells you |
66	|---|---|
67	| `<module>-classes.txt` | Stability of classes and properties |
68	| `<module>-composables.txt` | Restartable/skippable status and parameter stability |
69	| `<module>-composables.csv` | Same data in sortable form |
70	| `<module>-module.json` | Aggregate metrics |
71	
72	## 3. Fix only the proven parameter problem
73	
74	Pick the lightest fix that makes the type's immutability or equality semantics true.
75	
76	### Immutable collections
77	
78	If reports show collection interfaces on UI state, prefer `kotlinx.collections.immutable` at UI-state boundaries:
79	
80	```kotlin
81	// Before: unstable collection interfaces
82	data class UiState(val items: List<Item>, val tags: Set<String>)
83	
84	// After: immutable collection contracts
85	import kotlinx.collections.immutable.ImmutableList
86	import kotlinx.collections.immutable.ImmutableSet
87	
88	data class UiState(val items: ImmutableList<Item>, val tags: ImmutableSet<String>)
89	```
90	
91	Producers convert once at the boundary with `.toImmutableList()` / `.toImmutableSet()`.
92	
93	### `@Immutable` / `@Stable`
94	
95	- Use `@Immutable` when every property is effectively immutable and equality describes all observable state.
96	- Use `@Stable` for types whose mutable state is observable by Compose, typically via `MutableState`.
97	
98	Do not annotate to silence a report. A false stability promise can produce stale UI.
99	
100	### Third-party immutable types
101	
102	For types you cannot annotate but can truthfully treat as immutable, use `stabilityConfigurationFiles`:
103	
104	```kotlin
105	composeCompiler {
106	    stabilityConfigurationFiles.add(
107	        rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.file("compose_stability.conf"),
108	    )
109	}
110	```
111	
112	```text
113	java.math.BigDecimal
114	java.math.BigInteger
115	java.time.*
116	kotlinx.datetime.*
117	```
118	
119	Only list types you are willing to promise are immutable. Do not list mutable types such as `java.util.Date`.
120	
121	## 4. Stabilize lazy item inputs
122	
123	When lazy item recomposition comes from call-site churn, stabilize the values passed to each item instead of annotating models blindly.
124	
125	Hoist and remember per-item inputs that are stable for the item's lifetime:
126	
127	```kotlin
128	// ❌ BAD — new lambda instances when parent recomposes
129	items(list, key = { it.id }) { item ->
130	    RowCard(
131	        onClick = { onItemClick(item.id) },
132	        isHighlighted = { item.id == selectedId },
133	    )
134	}
135	
136	// ✅ GOOD — stable captures for this item instance
137	items(list, key = { it.id }) { item ->
138	    val onClick = remember(item.id) { { onItemClick(item.id) } }
139	    val isHighlighted = remember(item.id, selectedId) { item.id == selectedId }
140	    RowCard(onClick = onClick, isHighlighted = isHighlighted)
141	}
142	```
143	
144	Also hoist row position metadata (`isFirst`, `isLast`, corner radii) with `remember(index) { … }` when the value depends only on index — but do not expect this alone to fix back-writing or cross-row measurement bugs.
145	
146	Verify focus moves and insertions with recomposition-count assertions after hoisting.
147	
148	## Quick reference
149	
150	| Symptom | Diagnosis | Fix |
151	|---|---|---|
152	| Kotlin 2.0.20+ but old docs say unstable means non-skippable | Strong skipping changed the default | Check comparison semantics and instance churn instead |
153	| `unstable val items: List<Item>` | Interface collection | Use `ImmutableList<Item>` or another true immutable wrapper |
154	| `unstable val price: BigDecimal` | External immutable type | Add to stability config |
155	| `@Immutable` on a type with mutable internals | False promise | Fix the model or remove the annotation |
156	| Composable skips poorly despite strong skipping | New unstable instance each recomposition | Remember, hoist, or make the type stable/equality-based |
157	| Lazy items recompose on parent recompose despite unchanged data | New lambda or derived-value instance per parent recompose (§4) | Hoist per-item with `remember(item.id) { … }` |
158	| Reports not generated | Compose compiler plugin missing or flag not set | Apply `org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose` and enable destinations |
159	
160	## When NOT to apply
161	
162	- The issue is back-writing across phases or cross-row measurement reads. Use [`compose-state-deferred-reads`](../compose-state-deferred-reads/SKILL.md).
163	- The issue is a fast-changing `State` read in composition, such as scroll or animation. Use [`compose-state-deferred-reads`](../compose-state-deferred-reads/SKILL.md).
164	- The recomposition count matches real data changes.
165	- The bug is wrong data or stale state, not excess work.
166	- The code is test-only and readability is more important than report cleanliness.
167	
168	## Related
169	
170	- [`compose-state-deferred-reads`](../compose-state-deferred-reads/SKILL.md) - frame-rate state should often be read in layout/draw rather than composition.
171	- [`compose-recomposition-performance`](../compose-recomposition-performance/SKILL.md) - entry point when you are not sure which recomposition axis is involved.
172

2	name: compose-state-authoring
3	description: Use when writing or reviewing Jetpack Compose code with bare local var in a @Composable, remember { mutableStateOf(...) }, mutableStateListOf/mutableStateMapOf, or @ReadOnlyComposable.
4	---
5	
6	# Compose state authoring
7	
8	Not every `remember { … }` belongs here. This skill covers **local UI state** (`remember { mutableStateOf(…) }`, `mutableStateListOf` / `mutableStateMapOf`) and **`@ReadOnlyComposable`**. Other remembered APIs live in focused skills:
9	
10	- **`rememberCoroutineScope` / `rememberUpdatedState`** → [`compose-side-effects`](../compose-side-effects/SKILL.md)
11	- **`rememberLazyListState` / `rememberScrollState`** used for frame-rate reads → [`compose-state-deferred-reads`](../compose-state-deferred-reads/SKILL.md)
12	- **Focus navigation, focus state, `FocusRequester` ownership, behavior** → [`compose-focus-navigation`](../compose-focus-navigation/SKILL.md)
13	
14	## Core principle
15	
16	A `@Composable` is a function the runtime re-runs whenever its inputs change. Writing local state correctly comes down to two questions:
17	
18	1. **Mutable local state** — does my `var` survive recomposition *and* trigger it? If not, it silently resets on every recompose and writes are invisible.
19	2. **What kind of composable is this?** — do I *mutate* composition (place layout nodes, allocate slots, `remember`) or only *read* it? If only read, `@ReadOnlyComposable` lets the runtime skip work.
20	
21	Get either wrong and the symptoms are subtle: state that vanishes or optimizations that don't apply.
22	
23	## When to use this skill
24	
25	You're writing or reviewing Compose code and you see any of these:
26	
27	- `var x = …` inside a `@Composable fun` or any composable lambda (`Column { var x = … }`)
28	- A `@Composable fun` (or `@Composable get()` property accessor) whose body never lays anything out
29	- `@ReadOnlyComposable` on a function that calls `Text`, `Box`, `Column`, `remember`, …
30	- A composable whose visible state mysteriously resets on rotation, theme change, or recomposition
31	
32	## 1. `var` in a composable must be State-backed
33	
34	Recomposition re-executes the composable from the top. A local `var` is *re-initialized* on every pass — last recompose's value is gone, and writing to it doesn't tell the runtime to recompose.
35	
36	```kotlin
37	// ❌ BAD — counter resets on every recomposition; clicks never update the UI
38	@Composable
39	fun Counter() {
40	    var count = 0
41	    Button(onClick = { count++ }) { Text("$count") }
42	}
43	
44	// ❌ ALSO BAD — same rule applies inside composable content lambdas
45	@Composable
46	fun Wrapper() {
47	    Row {
48	        var count = 0         // Row's content lambda is @Composable too
49	        // …
50	    }
51	}
52	```
53	
54	```kotlin
55	// ✅ GOOD — `remember` survives recomposition, `mutableStateOf` triggers it
56	@Composable
57	fun Counter() {
58	    var count by remember { mutableStateOf(0) }
59	    Button(onClick = { count++ }) { Text("$count") }
60	}
61	```
62	
63	Two pieces and both matter:
64	
65	- `remember { … }` — *survives recomposition*. Without it the value is re-created each time.
66	- `mutableStateOf(…)` — *triggers recomposition*. Without it, mutations are invisible to the runtime.
67	
68	For collections, prefer `mutableStateListOf` / `mutableStateMapOf` (also `remember`-ed). They emit Snapshot reads on every read and Snapshot writes on every mutation. A `remember { mutableStateOf(mutableListOf<X>()) }` followed by `list.add(x)` will *not* recompose, because `MutableList.add` doesn't go through the State setter — you'd have to replace the value (`state = state + x`).
69	
70	### Back-writing snapshot state during composition
71	
72	**Back-writing** means writing observable state in a phase that triggers invalidation of an earlier (or the current) phase. Mutating `mutableState*` from the composable body back-writes into the same composition pass and schedules another. Do not rebuild derived data this way:
73	
74	```kotlin
75	// ❌ BAD — clear + putAll on every composition
76	val merged = remember { mutableStateMapOf<Key, ViewState>() }
77	merged.clear()
78	merged.putAll(parent)
79	merged.putAll(overlay)
80	
81	// ✅ GOOD — immutable snapshot remembered from inputs
82	val merged = remember(parent, overlay) {
83	    if (overlay.isEmpty()) parent else parent + overlay
84	}
85	```
86	
87	If the result is read-only for the current inputs, `remember(keys) { … }` is enough. See [`compose-state-deferred-reads`](../compose-state-deferred-reads/SKILL.md) for cross-row measurement and measure-phase fixes.
88	
89	### When this rule does NOT apply
90	
91	- **Inside `remember { … }`'s producer block.** That runs once per key change, not on every recompose. A local `var` there is fine: `val builder = remember { mutableListOf<X>().apply { var n = 0; … } }`.
92	- **In non-`@Composable` lambdas passed *out* of a composable.** `onClick = { var a = 0; … }` is a plain `() -> Unit`. Local vars there are normal Kotlin.
93	- **In plain (non-`@Composable`) helper functions.** Only composable scopes are affected.
94	
95	## 2. The `@ReadOnlyComposable` contract
96	
97	`@ReadOnlyComposable` declares that a composable *only reads* composition state — no `Text`, no `Box`, no `remember`, no layout nodes, no positional slots. The runtime can then skip allocating a group for the call, which matters for fast accessor-style composables (`MaterialTheme.colorScheme`, `LocalDensity.current`, design-system token accessors).
98	
99	The contract is **bidirectional**:
100	
101	- **Add `@ReadOnlyComposable`** when every composable call your body makes is itself `@ReadOnlyComposable` (or there are no composable calls at all — for example a function that only reads `LocalFoo.current` and returns a value).
102	- **Don't add it** if you call any non-read-only composable. The optimization assumes you don't participate in composition; violating that produces incorrect recomposition behaviour for callers.
103	
104	```kotlin
105	// ✅ GOOD — only reads composition locals, no layout, no remember
106	@Composable
107	@ReadOnlyComposable
108	fun appSpacing(): Dp = LocalDimensions.current.spacing
109	
110	// ✅ GOOD — composable property getter; same rule
111	val accent: Color
112	    @Composable @ReadOnlyComposable
113	    get() = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.tertiary
114	```
115	
116	```kotlin
117	// ❌ BAD — annotated read-only but lays out a Box; contract violated
118	@Composable
119	@ReadOnlyComposable
120	fun Header(): Int {
121	    Box {}                  // ← non-read-only composable call
122	    return 42
123	}
124	
125	// ❌ BAD — calls a normal composable from a read-only one
126	@Composable
127	@ReadOnlyComposable
128	fun computed(): Int = nonReadOnlyHelper()
129	```
130	
131	### Heuristic for "should I add it"
132	
133	If the body contains any of these, **do not** add `@ReadOnlyComposable`:
134	
135	- A layout call: `Box`, `Column`, `Row`, `LazyColumn`, `Text`, anything from `androidx.compose.foundation.layout` or `androidx.compose.material*`.
136	- A side-effect call: `LaunchedEffect`, `DisposableEffect`, `SideEffect`, `produceState`.
137	- `remember { … }` — positional memoization is composition state.
138	- A `@Composable` lambda invocation (`content()`).
139	- An invocation of a non-`@ReadOnlyComposable` composable function.
140	
141	If the body is only reading `Local*.current`, calling other `@ReadOnlyComposable` functions, or doing pure computation, **add** it.
142	
143	### When this rule does NOT apply
144	
145	- **`override fun` declarations.** The annotation is part of the contract; if the base isn't `@ReadOnlyComposable`, you can't make an override one. Refactor the base, or accept the override pays the group-creation cost.
146	- **Abstract declarations.** No body to check.
147	
148	## Related: side effects live in their own skill
149	
150	If a composable needs `LaunchedEffect`, `DisposableEffect`, `SideEffect`, `rememberCoroutineScope`, `rememberUpdatedState`, `snapshotFlow`, snackbar/navigation handling, analytics, or Flow collection, use [`compose-side-effects`](../compose-side-effects/SKILL.md).
151	
152	Focus splits by question: **navigation, focus state, `FocusRequester` ownership, behavior** → [`compose-focus-navigation`](../compose-focus-navigation/SKILL.md); **when** to call imperative `requestFocus` (effect timing, lifecycle, keys, API choice) → [`compose-side-effects`](../compose-side-effects/SKILL.md).
153	
154	This skill is about authoring Compose state correctly. `rememberUpdatedState` is effect capture state, not a general replacement for `remember { mutableStateOf(...) }`. Side effects have separate lifecycle and keying rules, and keeping them in one focused skill avoids two sources of truth.
155	
156	## Quick reference
157	
158	| Symptom | Diagnosis | Fix |
159	|---|---|---|
160	| `var x = …` inside `@Composable fun` body | Not recomposition-safe (§1) | `var x by remember { mutableStateOf(…) }` |
161	| `var x = …` inside `Column { … }` / `Row { … }` content lambda | Same — content lambdas are `@Composable` (§1) | Same fix |
162	| `remember { mutableStateOf(list) }` then `.add(x)` not recomposing | Mutation bypasses State setter | Use `mutableStateListOf`, or replace the value: `state = state + x` |
163	| `stateMap.clear(); stateMap.putAll(...)` in composable body | Back-writing composition → composition | `remember(keys) { derivedSnapshot }` |
164	| `@Composable fun` with no `Text`/`Box`/`remember`/effect calls | Could be `@ReadOnlyComposable` (§2) | Add `@ReadOnlyComposable` above `@Composable` |
165	| `@ReadOnlyComposable` function that calls `Box {}` / `Column {}` / a normal composable | Contract violation (§2) | Remove `@ReadOnlyComposable` |
166	
167	## When NOT to apply
168	
169	- **Tests** with `composeTestRule.setContent { … }` follow the same rules — they're production composables.
170	- **`produceState`** has its own producer block that runs in a coroutine; you don't need `LaunchedEffect` *inside* it.
171	- **`derivedStateOf`** has its own concerns around stability and equality — out of scope here; it's about *preventing* recomposition, not authoring state.
172	- **`override`s** of read-only-composable declarations: the annotation is fixed by the base; you can't add or remove it locally.
173	
174	## Red flags during review
175	
176	| Thought | Reality |
177	|---|---|
178	| "It's a small composable, the bare `var` is fine" | Recomposition can fire at any time. The reset is non-deterministic by design — and a single bug report later. |
179	| "I'll add `@ReadOnlyComposable` because the function looks simple" | "Simple" isn't the criterion. "Makes only read-only calls" is. |
180	| "I always reach for `LaunchedEffect` because it's the one I know" | Use `compose-side-effects`; effect API choice depends on lifecycle and keys. |
181	| "I'll just `.add()` to the remembered list" | A `mutableStateOf(List)` doesn't observe internal mutation — use `mutableStateListOf` or replace the value. |
182	| "The override needs `@ReadOnlyComposable` to match what it does" | If the base isn't `@ReadOnlyComposable`, you can't add it to an override. Refactor the base instead. |
183

2	name: compose-state-deferred-reads
3	description: Use when Jetpack Compose code reads scroll, animation, gesture, or other frame-rate State in composition, passes changing values across composable boundaries, uses value-form layout/draw modifiers, or back-writes observable state from a later phase into one that's already run.
4	---
5	
6	# Compose state deferred reads
7	
8	## Core principle
9	
10	State reads invalidate the phase that reads them. If a `State<T>` is read in a composable body, changes invalidate composition. If it is read in layout or draw, changes can invalidate only layout or draw. Frame-rate state such as scroll offsets, animations, and drag positions usually belongs in layout/draw, not composition.
11	
12	**Back-writing** is the symmetric failure mode: writing observable state from a phase that triggers invalidation of an earlier phase. Compose phases run composition → layout → draw. Writing snapshot-backed state from layout or draw to state read in composition invalidates composition; writing during composition to state read earlier in the same composition does the same. Both schedule extra work — often cascading into sibling lazy items.
13	
14	The fix is structural: keep the `State<T>` or a provider lambda and read the value inside a layout/draw callback; capture measurements in callbacks and apply them in the measure phase, not by reading measurement state in sibling composable bodies.
15	
16	## When to use this skill
17	
18	- `val x by animate*AsState(...)` is passed to `Modifier.offset(x = ...)`, `Modifier.size(...)`, `Modifier.graphicsLayer(...)`, or another value-form modifier.
19	- `LazyListState.firstVisibleItemScrollOffset`, `ScrollState.value`, `Animatable.value`, or gesture state is read in a composable body.
20	- A composable takes `scrollOffset: Int`, `progress: Float`, `dragOffset: Offset`, or similar frame-rate values.
21	- Recomposition counters climb during scroll, animation, or gestures even when data is stable.
22	- A composable body calls `stateMap[key] = …`, `list.addAll(…)`, or similar on every recomposition (back-writing composition → composition).
23	- One lazy item captures size with `onSizeChanged` / `onGloballyPositioned` and a sibling reads that height in composition (`Modifier.height(state.dp)`) — back-writing layout → composition.
24	
25	## 0. Back-writing
26	
27	**Back-writing** = writing observable state in one phase that triggers invalidation of an earlier (or the current) phase. Compose runs composition → layout → draw, so:
28	
29	- Writing snapshot state during composition that's read in the same composition.
30	- Writing snapshot state during layout (e.g. from `Modifier.layout`, `onSizeChanged`, `onGloballyPositioned`) that's read during composition.
31	- Writing snapshot state during draw that's read during composition or layout.
32	
33	In all cases the writer schedules extra invalidation passes — often cascading into sibling lazy items.
34	
35	Do not write to `mutableStateOf`, `mutableStateListOf`, `mutableStateMapOf`, or other snapshot-backed state from the composable body on every pass:
36	
37	```kotlin
38	// ❌ BAD — mutates observable map during composition; siblings recompose repeatedly
39	@Composable
40	fun MergeOverlay(parent: Map<Key, ViewState>, overlay: Map<Key, ViewState>): Map<Key, ViewState> {
41	    val merged = remember { mutableStateMapOf<Key, ViewState>() }
42	    merged.clear()
43	    merged.putAll(parent)
44	    merged.putAll(overlay)   // back-writing composition → composition
45	    return merged
46	}
47	
48	// ✅ GOOD — read-only merge; no composition-time writes
49	@Composable
50	fun MergeOverlay(parent: Map<Key, ViewState>, overlay: Map<Key, ViewState>): Map<Key, ViewState> =
51	    remember(parent, overlay) {
52	        if (overlay.isEmpty()) parent else parent + overlay
53	    }
54	```
55	
56	Prefer `remember(keys) { … }` for derived read-only snapshots. Reserve `mutableState*` writes for event callbacks (`onClick`) or effects — not for rebuilding derived data on every composition.
57	
58	Callbacks like `onSizeChanged` write *during layout*. That is only safe if no earlier phase reads the resulting state — see cross-row measurement below.
59	
60	### Cross-row measurement (layout → composition back-write)
61	
62	When row A measures and row B must match A's height, do not read A's captured size in B's composable body. `onSizeChanged` writes during layout; if B reads it in composition, layout has just back-written into composition:
63	
64	```kotlin
65	var anchorHeightPx by remember { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
66	
67	// ❌ BAD — B reads measurement state in composition; insertion/focus can double-recompose B
68	RowA(Modifier.onSizeChanged { anchorHeightPx = it.height })
69	RowB(Modifier.height(with(LocalDensity.current) { anchorHeightPx.toDp() }))  // composition read
70	
71	// ✅ GOOD — capture on A; apply on B in measure phase only
72	RowA(Modifier.onSizeChanged { if (it.height != anchorHeightPx) anchorHeightPx = it.height })
73	RowB(
74	    Modifier.decorateMeasureConstraints { incoming ->
75	        if (anchorHeightPx > 0) incoming.copy(minHeight = anchorHeightPx, maxHeight = anchorHeightPx)
76	        else incoming
77	    },
78	)
79	```
80	
81	`decorateMeasureConstraints` is a small layout helper (see [`compose-modifier-and-layout-style`](../compose-modifier-and-layout-style/SKILL.md)). While height is unknown, siblings use a fixed fallback in composition; once known, only layout invalidates — not an extra composition cascade.
82	
83	## 1. Prefer block-form modifiers
84	
85	Several modifiers have value forms and block forms. The value form receives values already read in composition; the block form can read during layout or draw.
86	
87	```kotlin
88	// Before: animated value read in composition by the `by` delegate
89	@Composable
90	fun SelectionPill(selectedIndex: Int) {
91	    val offsetX by animateDpAsState(120.dp * selectedIndex)
92	    Box(Modifier.offset(x = offsetX))
93	}
94	
95	// After: State is kept, value is read in the layout-phase offset block
96	@Composable
97	fun SelectionPill(selectedIndex: Int) {
98	    val offsetX = animateDpAsState(120.dp * selectedIndex)
99	    Box(
100	        Modifier.offset {
101	            IntOffset(offsetX.value.roundToPx(), 0)
102	        },
103	    )
104	}
105	```
106	
107	Common replacements:
108	
109	| Composition read | Deferred read |
110	|---|---|
111	| `Modifier.offset(x = animatedX)` | `Modifier.offset { IntOffset(animatedX.value.roundToPx(), 0) }` |
112	| `Modifier.graphicsLayer(translationY = y)` | `Modifier.graphicsLayer { translationY = yProvider() }` |
113	| `val radius by animateFloatAsState(...); drawBehind { drawCircle(radius = radius) }` | `val radius = animateFloatAsState(...); drawBehind { drawCircle(radius = radius.value) }` |
114	
115	The `drawBehind` block is already draw-phase; the important part is that the `State.value` read also happens inside that block.
116	
117	## 2. Pass providers across composable boundaries
118	
119	If the fast-changing value would cross a composable boundary, pass a provider lambda instead of a snapshot value:
120	
121	```kotlin
122	// Before: HomeScreen reads scroll offset in composition and passes the value down
123	@Composable
124	fun HomeScreen() {
125	    val listState = rememberLazyListState()
126	    LazyColumn(state = listState) {
127	        item { HeroImage(scrollOffset = listState.firstVisibleItemScrollOffset) }
128	    }
129	}
130	
131	@Composable
132	fun HeroImage(scrollOffset: Int, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
133	    AsyncImage(
134	        model = "...",
135	        modifier = modifier.graphicsLayer(translationY = -scrollOffset / 2f),
136	    )
137	}
138	
139	// After: the only read happens inside graphicsLayer
140	@Composable
141	fun HomeScreen() {
142	    val listState = rememberLazyListState()
143	    LazyColumn(state = listState) {
144	        item {
145	            HeroImage(
146	                scrollOffsetProvider = {
147	                    if (listState.firstVisibleItemIndex == 0) {
148	                        listState.firstVisibleItemScrollOffset
149	                    } else {
150	                        0
151	                    }
152	                },
153	            )
154	        }
155	    }
156	}
157	
158	@Composable
159	fun HeroImage(scrollOffsetProvider: () -> Int, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
160	    AsyncImage(
161	        model = "...",
162	        modifier = modifier.graphicsLayer {
163	            translationY = -scrollOffsetProvider() / 2f
164	        },
165	    )
166	}
167	```
168	
169	Suffix provider parameters with `Provider` when that clarifies the deferred-read contract.
170	
171	## 3. Other layout/draw read sites
172	
173	State reads can also be deferred inside:
174	
175	- `Modifier.layout { measurable, constraints -> ... }`
176	- Custom `Alignment.align(...)`
177	- `drawWithContent`, `drawBehind`, and other draw modifiers
178	- Block-form layer/layout modifiers such as `graphicsLayer { ... }` and `offset { ... }`
179	
180	Use these when the state changes where something is placed or painted. If the state decides *which composables exist*, it belongs in composition.
181	
182	## Quick reference
183	
184	| Symptom | Diagnosis | Fix |
185	|---|---|---|
186	| `val x by animateFloatAsState(...)` then `Modifier.offset(...)` | `by` reads in composition | Keep `State<Float>` and read `.value` in `offset {}` |
187	| `Modifier.graphicsLayer(translationY = animatedY)` | Property-argument form uses composition values | Use `graphicsLayer { translationY = ... }` |
188	| `Child(scrollOffset = listState.firstVisibleItemScrollOffset)` | Fast-changing value crosses boundary | `Child(scrollOffsetProvider = { ... })` |
189	| Draw block still recomposes every frame | Value was read before draw block | Move the `State.value` read inside the draw block |
190	| State chooses between different UI branches | Composition decision | Keep the read in composition |
191	| `mergedMap.putAll(overlay)` in composable body | Back-writing composition → composition | `remember(parent, overlay) { parent + overlay }` |
192	| Sibling `Modifier.height(measuredPx.toDp())` | Back-writing layout → composition | Measure-phase constraint decoration |
193	| Identity cache for read-only merge | Stale overlay risk | `remember(keys)` on immutable result |
194	
195	## When NOT to apply
196	
197	- The state controls which composables are emitted.
198	- The animation is one-shot, cheap, and clarity wins.
199	- You are writing tests where direct value assertions are simpler.
200	- Runtime evidence shows recomposition is not the bottleneck.
201	
202	## Related
203	
204	- [`compose-state-authoring`](../compose-state-authoring/SKILL.md) — when `mutableState*` belongs in composition vs callbacks.
205	- [`compose-state-holder-ui-split`](../compose-state-holder-ui-split/SKILL.md) — where state-holder vs plain UI split applies when passing providers/lambdas across boundaries.
206	- [`compose-stability-diagnostics`](../compose-stability-diagnostics/SKILL.md) — parameter stability and compiler reports.
207	- [`compose-modifier-and-layout-style`](../compose-modifier-and-layout-style/SKILL.md) — measure-phase constraint decoration helper.
