1	# Screen Structure in Jetpack Compose
2	
3	Screen-level structure — the architectural layer above individual composables. For slot / content-API authoring, see `compose/references/view-composition.md`; for M3 UX (touch targets, foldable postures, canonical layouts, M3 compliance), see `android-skills:android-ux`.
4	
5	This reference covers two screen-structure details that are easy to skip — making the content composable `private`, and keeping framework state in the UI rather than the ViewModel — not the basics of the screen/content split, `Scaffold`, or adaptive layouts.
6	
7	## Make the content composable `private`
8	
9	The screen/content split is common; making the **content composable `private`** (or `internal`) is the part that's easy to skip. The public screen composable wires the ViewModel; the private content composable is pure — testable, previewable, and impossible to accidentally hand a ViewModel from elsewhere.
10	
11	```kotlin
12	@Composable
13	fun UserDetailsScreen(userId: String, viewModel: UserDetailsViewModel = hiltViewModel()) {
14	    val uiState by viewModel.uiState.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
15	    LaunchedEffect(userId) { viewModel.loadUser(userId) }
16	    UserDetailsContent(uiState = uiState, onRetry = { viewModel.loadUser(userId) })
17	}
18	
19	@Composable
20	private fun UserDetailsContent(uiState: UiState, onRetry: () -> Unit) {   // private — pure, previewable
21	    when (uiState) { /* Loading / Success / Error */ }
22	}
23	```
24	
25	Pass **data, not the ViewModel**, down to child composables — `UserCard(user: User)`, never `UserCard(viewModel)` — or the child couples to the VM and stops being reusable and previewable.
26	
27	## Framework state stays in the UI composable — don't hoist it to the ViewModel
28	
29	`LazyListState`, `LazyGridState`, `ScrollState`, `PagerState`, `FocusRequester`, `BringIntoViewRequester`, `Animatable`, `TextFieldState`, and snackbar/drawer holders are **framework state** (Compose mechanics), not business state — keep them in the composable. Only **business state** (loaded data, screen mode, inputs that drive queries — anything with semantic meaning that must survive a configuration change) belongs in the ViewModel.
30	
31	```kotlin
32	// ✅ framework state in the composable; the animation clock is owned by the composition
33	@Composable
34	fun ConversationScreen(viewModel: ConversationViewModel = hiltViewModel()) {
35	    val uiState by viewModel.uiState.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
36	    val listState = rememberLazyListState()                 // stays here
37	    LaunchedEffect(uiState.scrollToTopSignal) { listState.animateScrollToItem(0) }
38	    ConversationContent(uiState, listState, onAction = viewModel::onAction)
39	}
40	
41	// ❌ LazyListState hoisted to the ViewModel — animateScrollToItem from viewModelScope runs on the
42	//    wrong clock/scope and breaks: the animation clock is tied to the composition, not the VM.
43	class ConversationViewModel : ViewModel() { val listState = LazyListState() /* … */ }
44	```
45	
46	See `compose/references/state-management.md` for the full clock/scope failure mode.
47

1	# Performance Optimization Reference
2	
3	## Two Axes: Stability and Phase
4	
5	Recomposition perf issues split into two independent axes — **parameter stability** (does Compose skip this composable?) and **state-read phase** (when does a state read trigger recomposition?). Decide which axis fits the evidence before applying fixes:
6	
7	- **Stability axis** — composable runs even though inputs didn't change. Diagnose with compiler reports (`*_composables.txt`, `*_classes.txt`) and the strong-skipping rules below. Fixes: stable types, `@Immutable`/`@Stable`, `stabilityConfigurationFiles`, immutable collections.
8	- **Phase axis** — composable runs because a state read happened in composition that could have happened in layout or draw. Diagnose with Layout Inspector recomposition counts. Fixes: provider lambdas, `Modifier.offset { }`, `Modifier.graphicsLayer { }`, `derivedStateOf`.
9	
10	The three frame phases the phase axis refers to: **composition** (runs composables, evaluates state reads — a read here invalidates the whole scope), **layout** (`measure`/`layout`; mutable reads here don't trigger recomposition — prefer `Modifier.offset { }` over `Modifier.offset()`), **draw** (`Canvas`/`DrawScope`).
11	
12	**Don't apply this skill when** recomposition tracks real data changes (correctness, not cost) or when no profiler/compiler signal suggests a problem. Premature stability annotations and `remember` wrapping cost more than they save.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## Recomposition Skipping with Compiler Reports
17	
18	The Compose compiler generates `$changed` bitmasks to detect state changes. Enable compiler reports **on demand** (opt-in via a Gradle property) so they don't generate on every build:
19	
20	```kotlin
21	// build.gradle.kts
22	composeCompiler {
23	    if (project.findProperty("composeReports") == "true") {
24	        reportsDestination = layout.buildDirectory.dir("compose_reports")
25	        metricsDestination = layout.buildDirectory.dir("compose_metrics")
26	    }
27	}
28	```
29	
30	Run with `./gradlew assembleRelease -PcomposeReports=true` when you actually want a report. Gating it keeps the default build fast.
31	
32	For a one-off audit against a repo you don't own, inject the config via `--init-script` instead of touching the target's build files:
33	
34	```kotlin
35	// compose-reports.init.gradle.kts
36	allprojects {
37	    afterEvaluate {
38	        extensions.findByType(org.jetbrains.kotlin.compose.compiler.gradle.ComposeCompilerGradlePluginExtension::class.java)?.apply {
39	            reportsDestination.set(layout.buildDirectory.dir("compose_reports"))
40	            metricsDestination.set(layout.buildDirectory.dir("compose_metrics"))
41	        }
42	    }
43	}
44	```
45	
46	Run with `./gradlew --init-script compose-reports.init.gradle.kts :app:assembleRelease`. No project-side changes; nothing to revert.
47	
48	What the generated files show:
49	
50	- **`*_composables.txt`** — each composable's restartability/skippability:
51	  ```
52	  restartable skippable fun MyComponent(name: String, onClick: Function0<Unit>)
53	  restartable fun UnstableComponent(items: List<Item>)  // NOT skippable — unstable param
54	  ```
55	- **`*_classes.txt`** — stability inference per class:
56	  ```
57	  stable class User { stable val name: String }
58	  unstable class ScreenState { unstable val items: List<Item> }
59	  ```
60	- **`*-composables.csv`** — programmatic view of skippability. **When reading the module-wide `skippable%`, filter out rows where `isLambda == "1"`** before computing the percentage. Zero-argument lambdas can't skip structurally (nothing to compare), so they pull the module number down even when every *named* composable is skippable. Named-only `skippable%` is the metric that maps to caller behaviour.
61	
62	With Kotlin 2.0.20+ and strong skipping on by default, the legacy "missing skippable means not skippable" reading is wrong — almost everything is skippable now. The diagnostic question is no longer "is this skippable at all?" but **"will these parameters compare the way I expect, and are callers creating new unstable instances every frame?"** (mechanics in *Strong Skipping Mode* below).
63	
64	When the report shows a composable as skippable but Layout Inspector shows it recomposing constantly, look at the **call site** — a caller probably allocates a new unstable instance every frame (`listOf(...)`, `Modifier.X.Y()`, an ad-hoc data class). Fixing instability turns `===` comparisons back into `equals()`:
65	
66	- **Unstable collection types** (`List`, `Set`, `Map`) — replace with `kotlinx.collections.immutable` equivalents (`ImmutableList`, …) so equality is meaningful.
67	- **All properties stable but the class isn't annotated** — same-module classes with all-stable properties are inferred stable automatically, so usually no action is needed; annotate `@Stable`/`@Immutable` only when inference can't see the type — and only if the contract genuinely holds, since a false promise causes skipped recompositions and stale UI. Don't annotate speculatively.
68	- **Inner types are themselves unstable** — fix the inner types first; the outer type then becomes stable. Can cascade several levels.
69	- **Cross-module boundary** — the compiler can't infer across modules; use `stabilityConfigurationFiles` (below).
70	- **Pragmatic opt-out** — `@Suppress("ComposeUnstableCollections")` per-function when the instability is harmless and refactoring isn't justified.
71	
72	### `@Immutable` vs `@Stable` — the boundary
73	
74	```kotlin
75	@Immutable data class Person(val name: String, val age: Int)
76	
77	@Stable
78	class UserViewModel : ViewModel {
79	    private val _state = MutableState(UserState())
80	    val state: State<UserState> = _state
81	}
82	```
83	
84	- **`@Immutable`** — every property is effectively immutable and `equals()` describes all observable state. The compiler skips whenever previous and current values are `equals`-equal. The stricter promise; lets it skip more aggressively.
85	- **`@Stable`** — for types whose mutable state is observable to Compose (typically via `MutableState`). You promise *any* observable change is flagged through a snapshot. Like every stable type it's compared with `equals()` (see *Strong Skipping Mode*); a holder that doesn't override `equals()` falls back to identity, so passing the same instance skips while observed snapshot changes still recompose. Right for ViewModels and snapshot-backed holders.
86	
87	**Don't annotate to silence a report.** A false stability promise produces *skipped recompositions and stale UI* — silent and hard to reproduce. If the contract doesn't hold, fix the type or live with the recomposition. (Never `@Stable` on a data class with mutable non-snapshot fields.)
88	
89	### Cross-module stability via `stabilityConfigurationFiles`
90	
91	The compiler can't infer stability for types from other modules or libraries (`java.time.*`, `java.math.BigDecimal`, `kotlinx.datetime.*`). Declare them globally:
92	
93	```kotlin
94	// build.gradle.kts
95	composeCompiler {
96	    stabilityConfigurationFiles.add(
97	        rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.file("compose_stability.conf")
98	    )
99	}
100	```
101	
102	```
103	# compose_stability.conf
104	java.math.BigDecimal
105	java.time.LocalDate
106	java.time.Instant
107	kotlinx.datetime.Instant
108	kotlinx.datetime.LocalDate
109	```
110	
111	Safer than `@Suppress` or wrapping (the promise lives in one reviewable file); more dangerous than annotations (no compile-time check that the type really is immutable). **Only list types you're willing to promise are immutable** — never `java.util.Date`/`Calendar` or anything backed by mutable state, or you get stale UI for the same reason a wrong `@Immutable` does.
112	
113	### The Five Stability Types in Compiler Reports
114	
115	The "stable vs unstable" model is too coarse; the compiler emits five classifications, and `runtime stable` in particular is **not a bug**.
116	
117	| Type | Meaning | Skipping behaviour |
118	|---|---|---|
119	| **Certain (stable)** | All properties known-stable at compile time | `equals()` comparison; skips when equal |
120	| **Runtime (stable)** | Stability depends on an inner type the compiler defers — a per-instance `$stable: Int` field is generated and checked at runtime | `equals()` if the runtime check passes; otherwise falls back to `===` |
121	| **Unknown** | Interface-typed parameter; concrete impl not visible | `===` (instance equality) — same instance skips |
122	| **Parameter** | A generic type parameter — depends on the call-site type argument | Resolved per call site |
123	| **Unstable** | Proven unstable (mutable field outside snapshots) | Strong skipping disabled; runs every time |
124	
125	The common mistake is treating **runtime stable** as a defect to annotate away. It isn't — the `$stable: Int` field is a valid compile-time-deferred classification. Adding `@Stable` on top only matters when the runtime check produces too many false negatives, and the right diagnostic for that is the inner type, not the wrapper.
126	
127	**Source verification:** the five types are defined in `androidx/compose/compiler/plugins/kotlin/analysis/Stability.kt`; the runtime `$stable: Int` field is generated by `ClassStabilityTransformer.kt`; the config format is parsed by `StabilityConfigParser.kt`; inference is in `StabilityInferencer.kt`.
128	
129	---
130	
131	## Strong Skipping Mode (Default in Kotlin 2.0.20+)
132	
133	Strong skipping is the default with the compiler shipped in Kotlin 2.0.20+. Drop the old "missing skippable means not skippable" mental model. The rules:
134	
135	- **Stable parameters** compare with `equals()`. Two equal instances skip.
136	- **Unstable parameters** compare with `===` (instance equality). The same instance skips; a new instance recomposes — even if `equals()` would return `true`.
137	- **Lambdas inside composables** are auto-remembered based on their captures. You don't need `remember { { ... } }` to keep an `onClick` stable.
138	
139	```kotlin
140	@Composable
141	fun Counter(count: Int, onClick: () -> Unit) {
142	    // 'onClick' is auto-remembered; stable across recompositions of the caller
143	    Button(onClick = onClick) { Text("Count: $count") }
144	}
145	```
146	
147	So a skippable composable that still recomposes is almost always a call-site problem — a fresh `List`, `Modifier` chain, or ad-hoc object on each parent recomposition — not a missing annotation on the callee. Verify the toolchain is recent enough (`kotlin = "2.0.20"` or newer); on older Kotlin the legacy "missing skippable" diagnosis still applies — plan the upgrade rather than papering over it.
148	
149	### Disabling Strong Skipping
150	
151	If a module depends on the old semantics during a migration, opt out via the feature-flag DSL (not the deprecated `enableStrongSkippingMode` property):
152	
153	```kotlin
154	composeCompiler {
155	    featureFlags.add(ComposeFeatureFlag.StrongSkipping.disabled())
156	}
157	```
158	
159	Transitional escape hatch only — re-enable as soon as the offending call sites are fixed.
160	
161	### Strong Skipping Doesn't Reach Non-`@Composable` Scopes
162	
163	Automatic lambda memoization happens inside `@Composable` functions only. Lambdas allocated in **non-composable scopes** still produce a fresh instance on every parent recomposition:
164	
165	| Scope | Why it's not memoized |
166	|---|---|
167	| `LazyListScope.items { … }` and its item lambdas | `items {}` is a regular Kotlin extension, not a composable |
168	| `Modifier.pointerInput(key) { … }` | `PointerInputScope.() -> Unit` is a suspend lambda |
169	| `object : Foo { override fun bar() = { … } }` | Anonymous object literal — Kotlin object scope |
170	| `Modifier.drawBehind { }`, `drawWithCache { }`, `drawWithContent { }` | `DrawScope.() -> Unit` is a regular lambda |
171	
172	Hoist these to a stable reference — usually a method reference (`vm::onClick`) or a `remember { ... }`:
173	
174	```kotlin
175	@Composable
176	fun ItemList(items: List<Item>, vm: ItemViewModel) {
177	    val onItemClick: (Item) -> Unit = vm::onItemClick  // stable method reference
178	    LazyColumn {
179	        items(items, key = { it.id }) { item ->
180	            ItemRow(item, onClick = { onItemClick(item) })  // lambda OK — inside @Composable item block
181	        }
182	    }
183	}
184	```
185	
186	### Inline Layouts Aren't Skippable
187	
188	`Row`, `Column`, `Box`, and other inline-marked composables are **not restartable or skippable**. Wrapping a `Row` "to make it skip" is a no-op — the compiler inlines the body into the parent's recomposition scope. The fix for a wasteful `Row` body is making the *parent* skippable so the inline body isn't re-executed.
189	
190	### Escape Hatches
191	
192	Reach for these rarely, with a justifying comment at the call site:
193	
194	| Annotation | Target | Use when |
195	|---|---|---|
196	| `@DontMemoize` | A lambda literal (`@Target(EXPRESSION)` — applies to the literal, not the type) | The lambda must allocate every call (fresh `MutableState` initializer, capture that mutates on equality) |
197	| `@NonSkippableComposable` | A composable function | The body must run every recomposition (telemetry, custom inspectors) |
198	| `@NonRestartableComposable` | A composable function | The function should inline into the parent's restart scope (library effect helpers) |
199	| `@ReadOnlyComposable` | A composable function | It only reads `CompositionLocal`s — never invalidates and never invalidates callers (e.g. `MaterialTheme.colorScheme`) |
200	
201	---
202	
203	## Defer State Reads to Layout/Draw Phase
204	
205	Reading state in composition triggers recomposition. Push reads to later phases:
206	
207	```kotlin
208	// BAD — reads in composition, recomposes on every offset change
209	@Composable
210	fun Box(offsetX: State<Float>) {
211	    val x = offsetX.value
212	    Box(modifier = Modifier.offset(x.dp, 0.dp))
213	}
214	
215	// GOOD — deferred read in layout phase
216	@Composable
217	fun Box(offsetX: State<Float>) {
218	    Box(modifier = Modifier.offset { IntOffset(offsetX.value.toInt(), 0) })
219	}
220	```
221	
222	### Provider Lambdas Across Composable Boundaries
223	
224	When state crosses a composable boundary, pass a **provider lambda**, not a snapshot value. Reading the value at the call site recomposes the parent on every change; reading inside the consumer's layout/draw block defers it.
225	
226	```kotlin
227	// WRONG — snapshot value crosses the boundary; parent recomposes every frame
228	@Composable fun HomeScreen(scrollOffset: Int) { HeroImage(scrollOffset = scrollOffset) }
229	
230	// RIGHT — provider lambda; HeroImage reads inside graphicsLayer's block
231	@Composable fun HomeScreen(scrollOffsetProvider: () -> Int) { HeroImage(scrollOffsetProvider) }
232	
233	@Composable
234	fun HeroImage(scrollOffsetProvider: () -> Int) {
235	    Image(
236	        painter = painterResource(R.drawable.hero), contentDescription = null,
237	        modifier = Modifier.graphicsLayer { translationY = -scrollOffsetProvider() / 2f },
238	    )
239	}
240	```
241	
242	The read happens inside `graphicsLayer { ... }` (draw phase), so the state read is recorded against the draw scope — changes invalidate only the layer, not `HeroImage` or `HomeScreen`.
243	
244	**The `by` delegate is the smell.** `val offset by scrollOffsetState` unwraps the snapshot at the read site. Keep the value as `State<T>` (or `() -> T`) so it can cross the boundary as a provider; once unwrapped, the only fix is re-wrapping.
245	
246	**Deferral sites** (reads stay out of composition), latest phase first:
247	- `Modifier.graphicsLayer { }` — draw phase, cheapest (translation/rotation/alpha, no relayout)
248	- `Modifier.offset { }` / `Modifier.layout { }` — layout phase (when child position affects siblings)
249	- `drawWithContent` / `drawBehind` / `drawWithCache` — draw phase (raw drawing)
250	- custom `Alignment.align(...)` — layout phase
251	
252	---
253	
254	## derivedStateOf — Reducing Recomposition Frequency
255	
256	When deriving an expensive computation from state, wrap in `derivedStateOf` to dedup downstream recompositions — two different inputs yielding the same result trigger only one downstream recomposition:
257	
258	```kotlin
259	// BAD — filters (and recomposes) on every items/query change
260	val filtered = items.filter { query in it.title }
261	
262	// GOOD — recomposes only when the filtered result actually changes
263	val filtered = remember(items, query) { derivedStateOf { items.filter { query in it.title } } }
264	LazyColumn { items(filtered.value) { /* ... */ } }
265	```
266	
267	---
268	
269	## remember with Keys — Configuration-Local Gotcha
270	
271	`remember` only for mutable state or expensive calculations — omit it for cheap work (string formatting, simple objects); over-wrapping costs memory. The non-obvious trap: if a `remember { }` body reads `LocalConfiguration`, `LocalDensity`, `LocalLayoutDirection`, or `LocalContext`, those **must** be in the key list, or the cached value silently goes stale on rotation, font-scale change, foldable posture, RTL flip, or density change.
272	
273	```kotlin
274	// WRONG — caches once at first composition; stays wrong forever after rotation
275	val columns = remember {
276	    val width = LocalConfiguration.current.screenWidthDp
277	    if (width >= 840) 3 else if (width >= 600) 2 else 1
278	}
279	
280	// RIGHT — key on the local that drives the computation
281	val configuration = LocalConfiguration.current
282	val columns = remember(configuration) {
283	    val width = configuration.screenWidthDp
284	    if (width >= 840) 3 else if (width >= 600) 2 else 1
285	}
286	```
287	
288	---
289	
290	## LazyList Performance
291	
292	Always provide `key` (enables item reuse and animations) and `contentType` for heterogeneous lists (without it, all items compete for one reuse pool):
293	
294	```kotlin
295	LazyColumn {
296	    items(items, key = { it.id }, contentType = { it.type }) { item -> /* ... */ }
297	}
298	```
299	
300	### Stabilize Per-Item Lambdas with `remember(item.id)`
301	
302	An item lambda that captures a per-item value (the item, an index, a per-item callback) is allocated fresh on every scroll, defeating strong-skipping for the row. Key it by stable id:
303	
304	```kotlin
305	// WRONG — fresh lambda every scroll; ItemRow re-runs even though `item` didn't change
306	items(items, key = { it.id }) { item -> ItemRow(item, onClick = { onItemClick(item) }) }
307	
308	// RIGHT — lambda keyed by stable id, remembered per item
309	items(items, key = { it.id }) { item ->
310	    val onClick = remember(item.id) { { onItemClick(item) } }
311	    ItemRow(item, onClick = onClick)
312	}
313	```
314	
315	### Prefetch and Cache Window (Foundation 1.9+ / 1.10+)
316	
317	Lazy layouts compose just outside the viewport during scroll to keep frame budget steady. Foundation 1.9+ exposes `LazyLayoutCacheWindow(ahead, behind)`; 1.10+ makes prefetch pausable under frame-deadline pressure.
318	
319	```kotlin
320	@OptIn(ExperimentalFoundationApi::class)
321	val state = rememberLazyListState(cacheWindow = LazyLayoutCacheWindow(ahead = 2, behind = 1))
322	```
323	
324	Tune `ahead` higher for tall items with slow images, lower (or 0) when items are cheap and prefetch bloats memory — touch this only when a profiler shows item composition spiking under scroll. For nested lazy layouts (a `LazyRow` per `LazyColumn` item), `NestedPrefetchScope` lets the outer list trigger inner prefetch ahead of the outer item entering composition.
325	
326	---
327	
328	## Subcomposition Pitfalls
329	
330	`SubcomposeLayout`, `BoxWithConstraints`, and `Scaffold` run a composition pass *during the measure phase* with a slot that depends on layout constraints. Powerful when needed; expensive when stacked.
331	
332	### `BoxWithConstraints` inside a `LazyColumn` item
333	
334	The highest-cost shape — every visible item runs its own subcomposition during measurement on every scroll:
335	
336	```kotlin
337	// WRONG — subcomposition per visible item, on every scroll
338	LazyColumn {
339	    items(items, key = { it.id }) { item ->
340	        BoxWithConstraints { if (maxWidth < 320.dp) CompactRow(item) else WideRow(item) }
341	    }
342	}
343	
344	// RIGHT — hoist the constraint decision to the screen level, pass a flag in
345	@Composable
346	fun ItemList(items: List<Item>) {
347	    BoxWithConstraints {
348	        val compact = maxWidth < 320.dp  // subcomposed ONCE per screen size
349	        LazyColumn {
350	            items(items, key = { it.id }) { item ->
351	                if (compact) CompactRow(item) else WideRow(item)  // plain conditional, no subcomposition
352	            }
353	        }
354	    }
355	}
356	```
357	
358	### Nested `Scaffold`
359	
360	`Scaffold` is a `SubcomposeLayout` — it subcomposes top bar, bottom bar, FAB, and content independently to measure inset padding. Nesting one inside another's content slot doubles the work and produces inset/padding bugs that look like spacing-arithmetic errors. Use one screen-level `Scaffold` per route; for nested sections, build from plain `Column` + `TopAppBar`.
361	
362	### Reuse with `SubcomposeSlotReusePolicy`
363	
364	When authoring a custom `SubcomposeLayout`, cap the reuse pool so old slot state isn't held indefinitely:
365	
366	```kotlin
367	SubcomposeLayout(
368	    slotReusePolicy = SubcomposeSlotReusePolicy(maxSlotsToRetainForReuse = 4),
369	) { constraints -> /* subcompose(...).first().measure(constraints) */ }
370	```
371	
372	For latency-sensitive content (a heavy section on a tab switch), `state.precompose(slotId, content)` composes ahead of the measure phase (`SubcomposeLayoutState`, Foundation 1.6+). **Lint signal:** AndroidX's internal `ComposableLambdaInMeasurePolicy` flags fresh composable lambdas allocated inside `subcompose(slotId)` blocks — hoist the lambda so the slot identity stays stable.
373	
374	**Source verification:** `SubcomposeLayout.kt`, `BoxWithConstraints.kt`, `Scaffold.kt` in `androidx.compose.foundation` / `androidx.compose.material3`.
375	
376	---
377	
378	## Baseline Profiles
379	
380	Baseline profiles tell R8 to pre-compile hot paths, cutting startup time and jank. Record with Jetpack Macrobenchmark (`MacrobenchmarkRule` + `measureRepeated`); profiles land in `baseline-prof.txt`.
381	
382	### `BaselineProfileMode.Require` vs `UseIfAvailable`
383	
384	When a measurement assumes a profile is installed, set `CompilationMode.Partial(baselineProfileMode = BaselineProfileMode.Require)`. The default `UseIfAvailable` **silently falls back** to measuring an unprofiled build when no profile is detected — producing CI numbers that look fine and lie about what users get.
385	
386	```kotlin
387	benchmarkRule.measureRepeated(
388	    packageName = "com.example.app",
389	    metrics = listOf(FrameTimingMetric()),
390	    iterations = 10,
391	    compilationMode = CompilationMode.Partial(baselineProfileMode = BaselineProfileMode.Require),
392	) { /* interact */ }
393	```
394	
395	In CI, `Require` turns a missing-profile bug into a loud failure — exactly what you want reviewing a baseline-profile PR.
396	
397	---
398	
399	## Measuring Performance
400	
401	**Layout Inspector → Show Composition Counts** (Tools > Layout Inspector, toggle in inspector) displays per-composable recomposition counts.
402	
403	### Argument Change Reasons (Android Studio Hedgehog+)
404	
405	The **Composition state** column classifies each parameter — map status to fix instead of guessing:
406	
407	| Status | Meaning | Likely fix |
408	|---|---|---|
409	| **Changed** | Parameter actually has a new value | The cause — check whether the upstream value should change this often |
410	| **Unchanged** | Equal, no contribution | Skip — not the source |
411	| **Uncertain** | Couldn't determine equality (unstable type, instance-equality fallback) | Stabilize the type so equality is meaningful |
412	| **Static** | Compile-time constant | Skip |
413	| **Unknown** | Interface-typed; concrete type hidden | Expose a stable concrete type, or ensure callers reuse instances |
414	
415	Most "why is this recomposing?" investigations resolve at **Uncertain** — an unstable type forces instance-equality, callers create new instances every parent recomposition, the composable runs every time. Fix the type; don't memoize the caller.
416	
417	For headless/CLI workflows, `android layout --diff --pretty` between two app states gives a JSON tree of changed nodes; combine with `SideEffect { Log.d(...) }` counters to correlate diffs with hot paths. **Macrobenchmark** `FrameTimingMetric()` reports frame times — target <16.67 ms for 60 fps.
418	
419	---
420	
421	## Symptom → Diagnosis → Fix
422	
423	The same surface symptom ("too many recompositions") routes to different fixes by axis. Reach for this before guessing stability vs phase:
424	
425	| Symptom | Diagnosis | Fix |
426	|---|---|---|
427	| Composable skips poorly despite strong skipping | New unstable instance each recomposition | Remember, hoist, or make the type stable |
428	| Draw block recomposes every frame | Value read before draw block | Move `State.value` read inside the draw block; use a provider lambda across boundaries |
429	| Regression after adding a type to a data class | Cross-module type is unstable | Add to `stabilityConfigurationFiles` or annotate `@Immutable` |
430	| LazyColumn item recomposes on every scroll | Lambda captured from parent | Cache with `remember(item.id)` or hoist the source out of the item |
431	| Animation triggers recomposition per frame | Animated state read in composition | Read inside `graphicsLayer { }` or `offset { }` |
432	
433	**Anti-patterns:** wrapping cheap values in `remember`; adding `derivedStateOf`/`remember` without Layout Inspector data (profile first); `@Stable` on a data class with a `MutableState` field (use `@Immutable` on a fully-immutable type instead).
434	
435	---
436	
437	## Other Techniques
438	
439	**`movableContentOf`** — move content between layout positions without disposing/recomposing it (preserves state):
440	
441	```kotlin
442	val movableContent = remember { movableContentOf { ExpensiveChild() } }
443	if (isExpanded) ExpandedLayout { movableContent() } else CollapsedLayout { movableContent() }
444	```
445	
446	**Composition tracing** — `trace("ExpensiveScreen") { /* body */ }` surfaces slow composables in Perfetto/systrace without logging.
447	
448	**`ReportDrawnWhen { items.isNotEmpty() }`** — marks first meaningful draw for startup metrics.
449	
450	**R8** — keep `minifyEnabled`/`shrinkResources` on; Compose ships default rules. Strip preview tooling in release: `-assumenosideeffects class androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.** { *; }`.
451	
452	**Zero-size DrawScope guard** — a composable's size can be zero during initial composition; guard divide-by-size math, and never `fillMaxSize()` a `Canvas` without a height constraint:
453	
454	```kotlin
455	Canvas(Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(200.dp)) {
456	    if (size.minDimension <= 0f) return@Canvas
457	    drawCircle(color = Color.Blue, radius = size.minDimension / 2)
458	}
459	```
460	
461	---
462	
463	## Compose Multiplatform Performance
464	
465	The stability/phase model and `derivedStateOf`/provider-lambda fixes are identical across platforms (shared composable logic). What differs is tooling and the rendering backend: Baseline Profiles / Macrobenchmark / Layout Inspector are **Android-only** (profile with JMH on Desktop, Instruments on iOS, browser DevTools on Web). iOS/Web rendering gotchas (ProMotion 120Hz Info.plist, Metal clip cost, synchronous image decode, Web full-canvas redraw + bundle size) live in `compose/references/platform-specifics.md`.

1	# Animation in Jetpack Compose
2	
3	This reference covers the animation traps, boundaries, and motion-token discipline, not the basics of `animate*AsState` / `AnimatedVisibility` / `AnimatedContent`. Always pass `label` for the inspector.
4	
5	## `AnimatedContent` — `contentKey` on shape, not payload
6	
7	For sealed wrappers (`UiState`, `Result<T>`), `AnimatedContent` re-triggers on *every* `targetState` change — so a payload change within the same shape (`Success([1,2,3])` → `Success([1,2,3,4])`) cross-fades when it shouldn't. Key on the shape:
8	
9	```kotlin
10	AnimatedContent(
11	    targetState = uiState,
12	    contentKey = { when (it) { is Loading -> "loading"; is Success -> "success"; is Error -> "error" } },
13	    label = "uiState",
14	) { state -> when (state) { /* Loading / Success / Error */ } }
15	```
16	
17	Now the cross-fade fires only on Loading↔Success↔Error, never on a Success-payload update. (In `transitionSpec`, combine exit+enter with **`togetherWith`** — the old `with` infix is deprecated — and `using SizeTransform(clip = false)` to animate the container size.)
18	
19	## Defer animated reads to the latest phase
20	
21	An animated value read in **composition** recomposes every frame; read in **layout** relayouts every frame; read in **draw** does neither. Prefer **lambda-based** modifiers (`graphicsLayer { }`, `offset { }`) over parameter-based (`graphicsLayer(alpha = …)`, `offset(x = …)`):
22	
23	```kotlin
24	val alpha by animateFloatAsState(if (visible) 1f else 0f, label = "alpha")
25	Box(Modifier.graphicsLayer { this.alpha = alpha })        // draw phase only — best (not Modifier.alpha(alpha))
26	
27	val xPx by animateIntAsState(if (moved) 300 else 0, label = "x")
28	Box(Modifier.offset { IntOffset(xPx, 0) })                 // layout phase (not Modifier.offset(x = xDp))
29	```
30	
31	For state crossing a composable boundary (parent `scrollOffset` → child), pass a **provider lambda** (`() -> Int`) and read it inside `graphicsLayer { }`, not a snapshot value — see `compose/references/performance.md`.
32	
33	## Use M3 motion tokens, not arbitrary durations
34	
35	`tween(durationMillis = 347)` has no design rationale; pin to the M3 ladder (and prefer `spring()` for interruptible, natural motion). Pair each duration tier with its easing:
36	
37	| Duration | ms | Easing token | Compose value |
38	|---|---|---|---|
39	| Short1–4 | 50 / 100 / 150 / 200 | Emphasized | `CubicBezierEasing(0.2f, 0f, 0f, 1f)` |
40	| Medium1–4 | 250 / 300 / 350 / 400 | EmphasizedDecelerate | `CubicBezierEasing(0.05f, 0.7f, 0.1f, 1f)` |
41	| Long1–4 | 450 / 500 / 550 / 600 | EmphasizedAccelerate | `CubicBezierEasing(0.3f, 0f, 0.8f, 0.15f)` |
42	| ExtraLong1–4 | 700 / 800 / 900 / 1000 | Standard / Decelerate / Accelerate | `FastOutSlowIn` / `LinearOutSlowIn` / `FastOutLinearIn` |
43	
44	Spring feel: stiffness `Low`(200) / `MediumLow`(400) / `Medium`(1500) / `High`(10000) = gentle→snappy; damping `NoBouncy`(1.0) / `LowBouncy`(0.75) / `MediumBouncy`(0.5) / `HighBouncy`(0.2) = none→cartoonish. Convert a Figma spring with `dampingRatio = damping / (2 * sqrt(stiffness * mass))`.
45	
46	## A few real anti-patterns
47	
48	- **`Animatable` created in composition** is recreated every recomposition — always `remember { Animatable(0f) }`.
49	- **Mutating animated state in the composition body** (`position = position + 10f` at the top level) is an infinite recomposition loop — drive it from a `LaunchedEffect`.
50	- **`updateTransition` for independent properties** couples animations that don't need syncing — use separate `animate*AsState`; reserve `rememberTransition` / `updateTransition` for properties that must animate in sync from one state.
51	
52	## Don't bolt `AnimatedContent` on navigation destination swaps
53	
54	Navigation already animates between destinations (`NavHost.enterTransition` / `exitTransition` / `popEnterTransition` / `popExitTransition`; in **Nav3**, `NavDisplay` owns its transitions). Wrapping a destination's whole content in `AnimatedContent` double-animates — the destination swaps, then the new content cross-fades on top.
55	
56	```kotlin
57	// WRONG — animates inside an already-animating destination
58	composable("list") { AnimatedContent(targetState = uiState) { … } }
59	
60	// RIGHT — let the nav host own destination transitions; use AnimatedContent only for intra-screen state
61	NavHost(navController, startDestination = "list",
62	    enterTransition = { slideInHorizontally { it } + fadeIn() },
63	    exitTransition = { slideOutHorizontally { -it / 3 } + fadeOut() },
64	) { composable("list") { ListScreen(...) } }
65	```
66	
67	See `references/navigation.md` for the Nav3 carry-over.

1	# Focus Navigation Reference
2	
3	Focus is the *primary* input model on TV, ChromeOS, keyboard, desktop, and any D-pad/remote device — clicks are secondary. A UI that looks right with a mouse can be unusable with a keyboard.
4	
5	Covers `FocusRequester`, `Modifier.focusable()`, `onFocusChanged`, `focusProperties`, key events, lazy-list focus restoration, focus traps, TV patterns, predictive back, and testing. Source: `androidx/compose/ui/focus/` and `androidx/compose/ui/input/key/`.
6	
7	## Core Principle
8	
9	**Make focus targets explicit, request focus after composition succeeds, and test with the input model users use** (D-pad/Tab, not tap). Three rules govern every decision here:
10	
11	1. **Don't fight the framework.** `Button`, `TextField`, `Modifier.clickable`, and `Modifier.selectable` already participate in focus. Add hooks only when behaviour demands it.
12	2. **Request focus from an effect, never the composable body.** `LaunchedEffect` guarantees composition finished and the node is attached.
13	3. **Restore focus by stable id, not by index.** Lists reorder; ids don't.
14	
15	## When To Reach For Focus APIs
16	
17	| Need | Add |
18	|------|-----|
19	| Normal button / text field / clickable focus | Nothing — already focusable |
20	| Programmatic initial or restored focus | `FocusRequester` + `Modifier.focusRequester(...)` |
21	| Visual/state reaction to focus changes | `Modifier.onFocusChanged { ... }` |
22	| Custom interactive surface not already focusable | `Modifier.focusable()` + role/semantics |
23	| Override directional navigation (D-pad/arrows) | `Modifier.focusProperties { ... }` |
24	| Handle hardware keys (Back, Enter, custom) | `Modifier.onPreviewKeyEvent` / `onKeyEvent` |
25	| Constrain focus to a region (modal, menu) | `FocusRequester` + `focusProperties` traps |
26	
27	If no row applies, the screen needs none of this. Don't sprinkle `focusRequester`/`onFocusChanged` on every button "just in case."
28	
29	## FocusRequester — Programmatic Focus
30	
31	```kotlin
32	val requester = remember { FocusRequester() }
33	
34	Button(onClick = onPlay, modifier = Modifier.focusRequester(requester)) {
35	    Text("Play")
36	}
37	
38	// Request from an effect, not the composable body:
39	LaunchedEffect(requester) { requester.requestFocus() }
40	```
41	
42	`requestFocus()` from the composable body races composition: the node may not be attached, the requester may be re-allocated on recomposition, or the call may run before layout. `LaunchedEffect` avoids all three.
43	
44	**Key the effect to the condition that makes the target exist** — not `Unit`:
45	
46	```kotlin
47	// BAD: fires once on initial composition, before items exist
48	LaunchedEffect(Unit) { firstItemRequester.requestFocus() }
49	
50	// GOOD: fires when items become available
51	LaunchedEffect(items.isNotEmpty()) {
52	    if (items.isNotEmpty()) firstItemRequester.requestFocus()
53	}
54	```
55	
56	**Target inside a lazy list:** items aren't composed until scrolled into view, so the requester's node may not be attached. Scroll first, then request: `listState.scrollToItem(i); requester.requestFocus()` — or keep the first visible item focused and let spatial search take over.
57	
58	**Special values:**
59	
60	```kotlin
61	focusProperties { up = FocusRequester.Default }   // defer to spatial search
62	focusProperties { left = FocusRequester.Cancel }  // block focus leaving this direction
63	```
64	
65	`Cancel` traps focus inside a region (modal, menu); `Default` opts back into spatial search. Source: `androidx/compose/ui/focus/FocusRequester.kt`.
66	
67	## Modifier.focusable() — Custom Interactive Surfaces
68	
69	A `Box` is not focusable; `Modifier.clickable` makes it focusable as a side effect. For an interactive surface without a click handler, add `focusable()` plus role/semantics so screen readers see what focus sees:
70	
71	```kotlin
72	Box(modifier = Modifier.focusable().semantics {
73	    role = Role.Button; contentDescription = "Drag handle"
74	})
75	```
76	
77	**Don't add `focusable()` to a `Column`/`Row` with interactive children — it swallows focus that should reach them.** A card that acts as one big button should use `Surface(onClick = ...)` or `Modifier.clickable`.
78	
79	## Modifier.onFocusChanged — React to Focus State
80	
81	`FocusState` properties:
82	- `isFocused` — this node is the focused target.
83	- `hasFocus` — this node *or any descendant* is focused (usually what you want for "this section is active").
84	- `isCaptured` — focus forcibly held (rare; modals).
85	
86	**Don't infer focus from selection.** A user D-pads through a list (focus moves) without selecting (commit pressed). Conflating them breaks every keyboard/TV interaction:
87	
88	```kotlin
89	// WRONG — focus conflated with selection
90	if (item.id == selectedId) Modifier.scale(1.05f)
91	
92	// RIGHT — observe focus separately
93	Modifier.onFocusChanged { state -> isFocused = state.isFocused }
94	```
95	
96	## Modifier.focusProperties — Override Spatial Navigation
97	
98	Default spatial search is good. Override only when the layout creates an unsolvable graph (off-screen item, two valid targets in one direction, a jump across the screen).
99	
100	```kotlin
101	val firstRow = remember { FocusRequester() }
102	
103	Column(modifier = Modifier.focusProperties {
104	    down = firstRow                 // "down" jumps directly to the first row
105	    left = FocusRequester.Cancel    // keep focus inside the column
106	}) {
107	    Header()
108	    LazyRow { item { FirstCard(modifier = Modifier.focusRequester(firstRow)) } }
109	}
110	```
111	
112	- Override **only the broken edges**; leave spatial search responsible for everything else.
113	- `FocusRequester.Cancel` traps; `FocusRequester.Default` returns to framework search.
114	- Overriding more than two directions on one node usually means the layout is wrong — fix the layout. Source: `androidx/compose/ui/focus/FocusProperties.kt`.
115	
116	## Key Events — onPreviewKeyEvent / onKeyEvent
117	
118	```kotlin
119	Modifier.onPreviewKeyEvent { event ->
120	    when {
121	        event.type == KeyEventType.KeyUp && event.key == Key.Back -> { onBack(); true }
122	        event.type == KeyEventType.KeyDown && event.key == Key.Escape -> { onDismiss(); true }
123	        else -> false
124	    }
125	}
126	```
127	
128	- **Return `true` only when consumed.** Returning `true` for everything swallows text input, accessibility shortcuts, and parent navigation. Default to `false`.
129	- `onPreviewKeyEvent` runs **before** children (intercept — e.g. a shortcut that should beat a focused `TextField`); `onKeyEvent` runs **after** (children first, the normal case). Dialog/back/escape usually wants preview, since focus is on a `TextField` below.
130	
131	| Key | Use |
132	|-----|-----|
133	| `Key.Back` | Hardware/browser back |
134	| `Key.Escape` | Dismiss dialogs/menus |
135	| `Key.Enter` / `Key.NumPadEnter` / `Key.DirectionCenter` | Activate focused item (D-pad center) |
136	| `Key.DirectionUp/Down/Left/Right` | D-pad / arrow navigation |
137	| `Key.Tab` | Focus traversal (Shift+Tab reverses) |
138	
139	**Throttle expensive D-pad responses at the boundary** — a TV remote fires 10+ events/sec. Throttle the response (scrolling, paging), not the handler:
140	
141	```kotlin
142	val scrollChannel = remember { Channel<Int>(Channel.CONFLATED) }
143	
144	LaunchedEffect(scrollChannel) {
145	    scrollChannel.receiveAsFlow().collectLatest { delta ->
146	        listState.animateScrollBy(delta.toFloat())
147	    }
148	}
149	
150	Modifier.onPreviewKeyEvent { event ->
151	    if (event.type == KeyEventType.KeyDown && event.key == Key.DirectionRight) {
152	        scrollChannel.trySend(itemWidth); true
153	    } else false
154	}
155	```
156	
157	Source: `androidx/compose/ui/input/key/KeyEvent.kt`.
158	
159	## Lazy List Focus Restoration
160	
161	When list content refreshes (pull-to-refresh, filter, paging), focus disappears unless restored. Restoring by index breaks the moment items reorder, insert, or delete — restore by stable id:
162	
163	```kotlin
164	@Composable
165	fun ArticleList(
166	    articles: ImmutableList<Article>,
167	    listState: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(),
168	) {
169	    // id -> FocusRequester, regenerated when ids change
170	    val requesters = remember(articles) { articles.associate { it.id to FocusRequester() } }
171	    // Track focused article so we can restore after refresh
172	    var lastFocusedId by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
173	
174	    LaunchedEffect(articles, lastFocusedId) {
175	        val id = lastFocusedId ?: return@LaunchedEffect
176	        val requester = requesters[id] ?: run {
177	            requesters.values.firstOrNull()?.requestFocus()  // focused id gone — fall back
178	            return@LaunchedEffect
179	        }
180	        val index = articles.indexOfFirst { it.id == id }
181	        if (index >= 0) {
182	            listState.scrollToItem(index)   // scroll into view first
183	            requester.requestFocus()
184	        }
185	    }
186	
187	    LazyColumn(state = listState) {
188	        items(articles, key = { it.id }) { article ->
189	            ArticleRow(
190	                article = article,
191	                modifier = Modifier
192	                    .focusRequester(requesters.getValue(article.id))
193	                    .onFocusChanged { if (it.isFocused) lastFocusedId = article.id }
194	            )
195	        }
196	    }
197	}
198	```
199	
200	**Fallback when the focused id no longer exists:** same id → nearest neighbour → first item → parent container. Pick one per screen and stick to it; the framework can't guess which the user expects.
201	
202	## Focus Traps — Dialogs, Modals, Menus
203	
204	A modal must keep focus inside until it closes, or D-pad/Tab walks the user out the back into the obscured content. Request initial focus on a button inside, and `Cancel` the edges:
205	
206	```kotlin
207	val confirmRequester = remember { FocusRequester() }
208	LaunchedEffect(confirmRequester) { confirmRequester.requestFocus() }
209	
210	Dialog(onDismissRequest = onDismiss) {
211	    Surface(modifier = Modifier
212	        .focusProperties {
213	            up = FocusRequester.Cancel; down = FocusRequester.Cancel
214	            left = FocusRequester.Cancel; right = FocusRequester.Cancel
215	        }
216	        .onPreviewKeyEvent { e ->
217	            if (e.type == KeyEventType.KeyUp && e.key == Key.Escape) { onDismiss(); true } else false
218	        }
219	    ) {
220	        Column {
221	            Text("Delete this item?")
222	            Row {
223	                Button(onClick = onDismiss) { Text("Cancel") }
224	                Button(onClick = onConfirm, modifier = Modifier.focusRequester(confirmRequester)) { Text("Delete") }
225	            }
226	        }
227	    }
228	}
229	```
230	
231	`Dialog` and `ModalBottomSheet` trap focus on Android **only if focus is inside them when they open** — always request initial focus on a child; never rely on the framework to do it.
232	
233	## TV and androidx.tv.material3
234	
235	For Android TV, prefer the TV-tuned components in `androidx.tv:tv-material` (package `androidx.tv.material3`) over regular Material 3 — they ship focus-aware visuals (rings, scale, elevation) and integrate with the leanback navigation model. For lists, use **Compose Foundation's `LazyColumn`/`LazyRow`**, which support D-pad focus on TV — do **not** use `androidx.tv:tv-foundation`'s `TvLazyColumn`/`TvLazyRow`/`TvLazyListState`: those lazy-list APIs are deprecated and have been removed from `androidx.tv.foundation` upstream. Gotchas:
236	
237	- **Touch targets don't apply** — D-pad jumps don't need 48dp; visual focus indication (ring/scale/glow) matters more.
238	- **No hover on TV** — `hover ≠ focus`.
239	- **`Modifier.clickable` registers for D-pad center** automatically; no custom activation handler needed.
240	- **Don't trap horizontal focus on rows** — a row that swallows `left`/`right` at its edges feels broken. Let edges escape to siblings.
241	
242	## Predictive Back Focus Restoration (Android 14+)
243	
244	`PredictiveBackHandler` animates the back gesture but does **not** restore focus on the destination — the source screen does. Its `rememberSaveable` `lastFocusedId` (see the lazy-list recipe above) drives restoration when it recomposes after back; the detail screen's job is just to navigate. See `compose/references/animation.md` for the visual side.
245	
246	## Testing Focus
247	
248	Drive the same input model users use — a click test on a TV/keyboard UI proves nothing. Use `performKeyInput { keyDown(Key.DirectionDown); keyUp(...) }` and assert ownership with `assertIsFocused()` (screenshot tests are for the *appearance* of focus — ring/scale/elevation — not ownership).
249	
250	```kotlin
251	@Test fun `D-pad down from header focuses first item`() {
252	    composeTestRule.setContent { AppTheme { BrowseScreen(uiState = previewSuccessState()) } }
253	    composeTestRule.onNodeWithTag("header").performKeyInput { keyDown(Key.DirectionDown); keyUp(Key.DirectionDown) }
254	    composeTestRule.onNodeWithTag("first-item").assertIsFocused()
255	}
256	```
257	
258	The load-bearing restoration test proves **id-not-index**: focus an item, refresh with a `shuffled()` list (same ids, new order), assert the *same id* is focused again. See `android-skills:android-testing` for the broader test-shape decision.
259	
260	## Review Red Flags
261	
262	- "It focuses when I tap it" for a TV/ChromeOS/keyboard screen — drive D-pad/Tab instead.
263	- Initial focus works with fixed data but fails after load/refresh — usually `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` instead of keying to the loaded condition.
264	- Focus inferred from selection state.
265	- `focusable()` on a `Column`/`Row` with interactive children (swallows focus).
266	- `Modifier.onPreviewKeyEvent { _ -> true }` — swallows unhandled keys.
267	- A modal opens without requesting focus on a child inside it.
268	- Lazy-list refresh with no restoration recipe.
269	
270	## See also
271	
272	For test-shape decisions and semantics-first selectors, see `android-skills:android-testing`. For predictive-back animation, see `compose/references/animation.md`. For the semantics layer (separate from focus traversal), see `compose/references/accessibility.md`.
273

1	# Lists and Scrolling in Jetpack Compose
2	
3	This reference covers the performance traps and hardening details of lazy lists, not the basics of `LazyColumn` / `LazyRow`, the `items` DSL, keys, or grids.
4	
5	## The `indexOf()`-in-item-factory O(n²) trap
6	
7	Calling `indexOf` / `lastIndexOf` / `indexOfFirst { }` on the source list **inside** the item lambda is O(n) per item, so a single scroll pass costs O(n²) over the list. It's a convincing trap because the lookup is often genuinely needed ("highlight the active item").
8	
9	```kotlin
10	// WRONG — O(n²): each item rescans the whole list for its own position, on every scroll recomposition
11	items(items, key = { it.id }) { item ->
12	    val isActive = items.indexOf(item) == activeIndex      // O(n) per item
13	    ItemRow(item, isActive)
14	}
15	
16	// RIGHT — itemsIndexed gives the index for free
17	itemsIndexed(items, key = { _, it -> it.id }) { position, item -> ItemRow(item, position == activeIndex) }
18	
19	// RIGHT (lookup is by id, not index) — build a Map once, outside the lambda
20	val byId = remember(items) { items.associateBy { it.id } }
21	items(items, key = { it.id }) { item -> ItemRow(item, byId[activeId] === item) }   // O(1)
22	```
23	
24	(LazyList *crash* patterns — `indexOf` → `IndexOutOfBoundsException`, duplicate/colliding keys + the dedup-index fix, `derivedStateOf` driving a collection count — live in `compose/references/production-crash-playbook.md`, §2/§4/§5/§8.)
25	
26	## Keys: never build a new object in the key lambda
27	
28	A stable-id key is the easy part; the trap is computing a *new object* in the key lambda, which defeats it (the key changes every recomposition):
29	
30	```kotlin
31	items(users, key = { User(it.id, it.name) }) { … }   // WRONG — new object every recomposition
32	items(users, key = { it.id }) { … }                  // RIGHT — primitive, stable id
33	```
34	
35	## `animateItem()` needs stable keys
36	
37	`items(list, key = { it.id })` gives each item identity across recompositions — which is exactly what makes `animateItem()` (per-item add/remove/move animation), efficient diffing, and per-item state preservation work. Reach for `itemsIndexed` only when you genuinely need the index for display.
38	
39	```kotlin
40	items(items, key = { it.id }) { item ->
41	    ItemRow(item, modifier = Modifier.animateItem(
42	        fadeInSpec = tween(250),
43	        placementSpec = spring(Spring.DampingRatioLowBouncy, Spring.StiffnessMediumLow),
44	        fadeOutSpec = tween(150),
45	    ))
46	}
47	```
48	
49	## `ReportDrawnWhen` for startup metrics
50	
51	Signal that the first meaningful content is visible so Android vitals measures TTID/TTFD correctly:
52	
53	```kotlin
54	@Composable
55	fun ConversationListScreen(items: List<Conversation>) {
56	    ReportDrawnWhen { items.isNotEmpty() }
57	    LazyColumn { items(items, key = { it.id }) { ConversationRow(it) } }
58	}
59	```
60	
61	## Infinite scroll — derive the trigger, and test across OEMs
62	
63	```kotlin
64	val shouldLoadMore by remember {
65	    derivedStateOf {
66	        val last = listState.layoutInfo.visibleItemsInfo.lastOrNull()?.index ?: 0
67	        last >= listState.layoutInfo.totalItemsCount - PREFETCH_THRESHOLD   // e.g. 5
68	    }
69	}
70	LaunchedEffect(shouldLoadMore) { if (shouldLoadMore) viewModel.loadNextPage() }
71	```
72	
73	Some OEMs (notably Samsung) deliver scroll events differently and trigger lazy-load with fewer confirmations — make `PREFETCH_THRESHOLD` configurable and test on multiple devices. (For full Paging-3-backed infinite scroll, see `android-skills:paging`.)
74	
75	**Two scroll containers fighting:** don't wrap a lazy child in a `verticalScroll` modifier, or nest a `Column(verticalScroll)` inside a `LazyColumn` item — use nested lazy composables, or a `nestedScroll` connection for coordinated scroll.
76
